definition_zh: 预言；预示；预告
definition_en: to say or show that something will happen before it does
core_image: 事情还没发生，话已经先传到了人耳中
scene: 村里的老人看了看云层，说这场雨很快就会停。The village elders could foretell that the rain would soon end.
sceneCN: 这里「foretell」是「预言、预示」（第 1 个义项：在事情发生前说出它将发生）；句意：老人看了看云层，说这场雨很快就会停。

pos.zh: 预言；预示；预告

derivatives.zh: 由 foretell 加 -er 构成，义为「预言者」
由 foretell 加 -ing 构成，义为「预言；预告」

senses.title: To announce an event before it happens
senses.definition: to say that an event will happen before it takes place
senses.definitionCN: 在事件发生之前说出它将会发生
senses.example: No one can foretell what the weather will be next month.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人能预言下个月的天气。
senses.why: Fore- supplies before and tell supplies the act of saying, so foretell is literally to tell beforehand.
senses.whyCN: fore- 提供「在前」的意思，tell 提供「说出」的动作，所以 foretell 字面上就是「事先说出」。

senses.title: To be a sign of something to come
senses.definition: to be a sign that something will happen or is coming
senses.definitionCN: 成为某事将要发生或即将到来的迹象
senses.example: Dark clouds foretell a heavy storm.
senses.exampleCN: 乌云预示着大风暴。
senses.why: A sign speaks before the event, so the word moves from a person telling to a thing announcing.
senses.whyCN: 征兆在事件之前「说话」，于是这个词从人「说出」扩展到事物「预示」。

senses.title: To speak as a prophet
senses.definition: to reveal future events as a prophet or seer, often by divine inspiration
senses.definitionCN: 像先知或预言者那样揭示未来之事，常指受神启而说
senses.example: The prophet foretold the fall of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 先知预言了这座城市的陷落。
senses.why: Religious use keeps the older picture of a message received and passed on ahead of time.
senses.whyCN: 宗教用法保留了更古老的画面：先接到消息，再提前把它传出去。

intro.en: Foretell is the Old English verb foretellan, built from fore, before, and tellan, to tell or count.
intro.cn: foretell 是古英语动词 foretellan，由 fore（在前）与 tellan（讲述、计数）构成。

items.en: Fore means before or beforehand.
items.cn: fore 意为「在……之前」或「事先」。

items.en: Tellan means to tell, relate, or count.
items.cn: tellan 意为讲述、叙述或计数。

items.en: Foretellan means to foretell, to say something before it happens.
items.cn: foretellan 意为预言，即在事情发生之前把它说出来。

items.en: Foretellen keeps the sense of announcing an event in advance.
items.cn: foretellen 保留了提前宣布事件的含义。

items.en: Modern English keeps foretell mainly in literary, biblical, and formal use, beside predict and forecast.
items.cn: 现代英语主要把 foretell 保留在文学、圣经与正式语境中，与 predict、forecast 并存。

note.en: Foretell shares the fore- family with forecast and forethought, and it stands near predict and prophesy.
note.cn: foretell 与 forecast、forethought 同属 fore- 词族，意义上靠近 predict 与 prophesy。

entries.definition: said or announced beforehand
entries.definitionCN: 预言了；事先说出的（foretell 的过去式与过去分词）

entries.definition: the act of announcing future events
entries.definitionCN: 预言；预告

entries.definition: a person who foretells
entries.definitionCN: 预言者

entries.definition: to say what will happen in the future
entries.definitionCN: 预测；预言

entries.definition: to speak of future events as a prophet
entries.definitionCN: 作预言；先知式地预言

entries.definition: to predict a future condition from present signs
entries.definitionCN: 预报；预测

normalIntro.en: Foretell is fore plus tell: to tell an event before it happens.
normalIntro.cn: foretell 就是 fore 加 tell：在事情发生之前把它说出来。

normal.en: Fore means before; tell means to say; so foretell is to say before.
normal.cn: fore 是「在前」，tell 是「说出」，所以 foretell 就是事先说出。

normal.en: The past form is foretold, not foretelled, because tell has an irregular past.
normal.cn: 过去式是 foretold，而不是 foretelled，因为 tell 的过去式不规则。

normal.en: A prophet foretells; a weather sign can also foretell a storm.
normal.cn: 先知会预言；天气征兆也能预示风暴。

normal.en: Foretell is mostly literary today; predict and forecast cover ordinary use.
normal.cn: 今天 foretell 多用于文学语境，日常表达多用 predict 与 forecast。

normal.en: Compare foretell with forecast: foretell is about events, forecast is about weather or numbers.
normal.cn: 对比 foretell 与 forecast：foretell 多指事件，forecast 多指天气或数值。

abstract.en: Imagine a messenger running ahead of an army to announce its arrival.
abstract.cn: 想象一名信使跑在军队前面，提前宣布军队的到来。

abstract.en: See dark clouds writing a warning across the sky before rain falls.
abstract.cn: 想象乌云在天空写下警告，随后雨才落下。

abstract.en: Picture a prophet on a hill speaking to a crowd about a city that has not yet fallen.
abstract.cn: 想象山上的先知向人群讲述一座尚未陷落的城市。

examples.en: No one can foretell what the weather will be next month.
examples.cn: 没有人能预言下个月的天气。

examples.en: Dark clouds foretell a heavy storm.
examples.cn: 乌云预示着大风暴。

examples.en: The prophet foretold the fall of the city.
examples.cn: 先知预言了这座城市的陷落。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛太欧」——「佛」提前把话「tell」出来，就是预言；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 fore（在前）加 tellan（讲述）→ foretellan → 中古英语 foretellen → 现代英语 foretell，核心义「事先说出」。

sensesIntro.en: Foretell moves from a person saying what will happen, to a sign pointing to what is coming, and finally to prophetic speech.
sensesIntro.cn: foretell 从人说出将要发生的事，转到征兆指向即将到来之事，最后转到先知式的预言。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a messenger who speaks before the event arrives.
core.cn: 核心意象：事件到来之前，信使先把消息说出口。

branches.en: The general sense is a person saying what will happen.
branches.cn: 一般义是人说出将会发生的事。

branches.en: The sign sense lets an object announce what is coming.
branches.cn: 征兆义让事物本身预告即将到来之事。

branches.en: The prophetic sense frames the message as inspired.
branches.cn: 先知义把消息说成受神启而来。

branches.en: Both a speaker and a sign can announce an event before it arrives.
branches.cn: 说话者与征兆都能在事件到来之前发出预告。

branches.en: Prophecy is the solemn, inspired form of telling beforehand.
branches.cn: 先知式预言是「事先说出」的庄重、受启发形式。

intro.en: Foretell combines the Old English prefix fore- with tell; the family includes foreteller, foretelling, and forecast.
intro.cn: foretell 把古英语前缀 fore- 与 tell 结合，词族包括 foreteller、foretelling 与 forecast。

latinIntro.en: Foretell is wholly Germanic and has no Latin root, so no Latin kin are listed.
latinIntro.cn: foretell 完全属于日耳曼语，没有拉丁词根，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: Fore- places the action before the event.
items.exampleCN: fore- 把动作放在事件之前。

items.example: Tell supplies the speaking half of foretell.
items.exampleCN: tell 提供 foretell 中「说」的一半。

items.meaning: to say something before it happens
items.exampleCN: foretell 由 fore- 与 tell 组合而成。

items.meaningCN: 预言了（过去式与过去分词）
items.example: Foretold is the irregular past of foretell.
items.exampleCN: foretold 是 foretell 的不规则过去式。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms a noun of action.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成表示动作的名词。
后缀 -er 指从事这一动作的人。

items.example: Forecast shares fore- but uses cast.
items.exampleCN: forecast 共享 fore-，但核心是 cast。

items.meaning: careful thought about what may happen
items.example: Forethought shares fore- but uses thought.
items.exampleCN: forethought 共享 fore-，但核心是 thought。

definition_zh: （作为惩罚）丧失；被没收；罚金；弃权
definition_en: to lose money, property, or a right because of a mistake, a crime, or a rule
core_image: 裁判从犯规球员手里收回奖杯，放到罚物台上
scene: 比赛因故取消，主队没有出场，按规则被判失去参赛资格。The home team forfeited the match when it refused to play.
sceneCN: 这里 forfeit 是「（比赛）弃权、被判负」（第 7 个义项：未出场而失去比赛资格）；句意：比赛因故取消，主队拒绝出场，于是被判弃权。

pos.zh: 丧失；被没收；放弃（权利）
罚金；被没收之物；（游戏中的）罚物

derivatives.zh: forfeit 加名词后缀 -ure 构成，指「丧失、没收」这一法律后果
forfeit 加 -able 构成，指「可被罚没的、可丧失的」
non- 加 forfeiture 构成，保险术语，指「不丧失权益」条款

senses.title: To lose something as a legal penalty
senses.definition: to lose money, land, or goods because a law or contract says they must be taken away
senses.definitionCN: 因法律或合同规定而被夺走钱财、土地或货物
senses.example: The court made the company forfeit the land it had bought illegally.
senses.exampleCN: 法院裁定该公司丧失其非法购入的土地。
senses.why: The Latin verb forisfacere meant to act outside the law, so the thing gained outside the law is taken away.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 forisfacere 意为「在法度之外行事」，所以在法度之外取得的财物会被收走。

senses.title: To lose an advantage by a foolish act
senses.definition: to lose something valuable, such as trust or a chance, because of what one has done
senses.definitionCN: 因为自己的所作所为而失去信任、机会等宝贵之物
senses.example: By lying on the form, he forfeited the trust of his colleagues.
senses.exampleCN: 他在表格上撒谎，因而失去了同事的信任。
senses.why: A forfeit is always a loss that follows a wrong act, so the wrong and the loss stay tied together.
senses.whyCN: forfeit 所指的损失总跟着某个错误行为，错误与损失被绑在一起。

senses.title: A sum paid as a penalty
senses.definition: a sum of money that must be paid as a punishment for breaking a rule
senses.definitionCN: 因违反规则而必须缴纳的一笔钱
senses.example: Latecomers must pay a forfeit of ten pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 迟到者必须缴纳十英镑罚金。
senses.why: The noun turns the act of losing into the money that is handed over.
senses.whyCN: 名词义把「丧失」这个动作转成被交出去的那笔钱。

senses.title: Something given up as a security
senses.definition: an object or amount handed over in advance and kept if a promise is broken
senses.definitionCN: 事先交出、若违约就被扣下的一笔钱或一件物品
senses.example: The key deposit is a forfeit if the tenant leaves early.
senses.exampleCN: 如果房客提前搬走，钥匙押金就成了被没收的抵押物。
senses.why: A pledge works like a hostage: it is held until the promise is kept, then kept as a forfeit when it fails.
senses.whyCN: 抵押物像人质，守约时归还，失约时就被留下当作罚没物。

senses.title: To lose a right by missing a condition
senses.definition: to lose a legal right or claim because a required step was not taken in time
senses.definitionCN: 因没有按时完成必要步骤而失去法定权利或请求权
senses.example: The buyer forfeited the warranty by repairing the machine himself.
senses.exampleCN: 买方自行修理机器，因而失去了保修权利。
senses.why: Legal systems attach deadlines to rights, and once the step is missed the right falls away like an object out of reach.
senses.whyCN: 法律给权利设定时限，一旦错过步骤，权利就像够不着的物件一样滑走。

senses.title: To be deprived of life or liberty
senses.definition: to lose life, freedom, or rank as the settled punishment for a grave offence
senses.definitionCN: 因重罪而被剥夺生命、自由或身份，作为既定惩罚
senses.example: The rebel forfeited his life for treason.
senses.exampleCN: 那名叛乱者因叛国罪被处死。
senses.why: This is the harshest reading of the core image: when the penalty is total, the thing taken away is life itself.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心意象最严厉的读法：当惩罚是彻底的，被拿走的就是生命本身。

senses.title: To concede a game without playing
senses.definition: to lose a match or contest by officially withdrawing or failing to appear
senses.definitionCN: 因正式退出或未出场而被判输掉比赛
senses.example: The visiting side forfeited the final rather than play in the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 客队宁愿弃权也不在暴风雨中比赛，因此被判负。
senses.why: Sport turns the legal penalty into a scoreboard result: the loss is recorded before a ball is kicked.
senses.whyCN: 体育把法律式惩罚变成记分结果：球还没开踢，失利就已经记在账上。

senses.title: A playful penalty in a party game
senses.definition: a small task or object demanded from a player who loses or breaks a rule in a game
senses.definitionCN: 游戏中输掉或违规的人被要求完成的小任务或交出的物件
senses.example: The loser had to sing a song as a forfeit.
senses.exampleCN: 输的人得唱一首歌作为惩罚。
senses.why: The core image softens into play: the thing taken away is no longer a right, only a small embarrassment.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象在游戏里变轻：被拿走的不是权利，而是一点小小的难堪。

intro.en: Forfeit comes from Old French forfait, a crime or misdeed, from forfaire, to transgress, built on Latin foris, outside, and facere, to do.
intro.cn: forfeit 来自古法语 forfait（罪行、过失），源于 forfaire（越界行事），由拉丁语 foris（外面）与 facere（做）构成。

items.en: Foris means outside or out of doors, and facere means to do or make.
items.cn: foris 意为「在外面、户外」，facere 意为「做、制作」。

items.en: Forisfacere joins them into to act outside the law, that is, to transgress.
items.cn: forisfacere 把两者合成「在法度之外行事」，也就是越界、违法。

items.en: Forfait names the crime itself, and forfaire names the act of committing it.
items.cn: forfait 指罪行本身，forfaire 指犯下罪行的行为。

items.en: Forfeit enters English as both a crime and the penalty for it.
items.cn: forfeit 进入英语时既指罪行，也指由此而来的惩罚。

items.en: The word widens from crime to the loss of property or rights that follows.
items.cn: 这个词从「罪行」扩大到随之而来的财产或权利丧失。

items.en: Sport, games, and contract law give forfeit its current range.
items.cn: 体育、游戏与合同法赋予 forfeit 今天的义域。

note.en: Forfeit is the loss that follows a wrong; its family includes forfeiture, and its neighbours are words for losing or surrendering.
note.cn: forfeit 是因过错而导致的丧失，同族词包括 forfeiture，近邻则是表示失去或交出的词。

entries.definition: the loss of property or a right as a penalty
entries.definitionCN: 因惩罚而丧失财产或权利

entries.definition: able to be lost or taken away as a penalty
entries.definitionCN: 可被罚没的；可丧失的

entries.definition: an excessive amount, especially of food
entries.definitionCN: 过量，尤指饮食过度；只是拼写与 forfeit 相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to no longer have something
entries.definitionCN: 失去

entries.definition: to give up something to another
entries.definitionCN: 交出；放弃

entries.definition: to give up something valuable for a purpose
entries.definitionCN: 牺牲；舍弃

normalIntro.en: Forfeit is a loss ordered by a rule: the thing is removed because a wrong was done.
normalIntro.cn: forfeit 是按规则判定的丧失：因为做了错事，东西被拿走。

normal.en: A team that does not appear forfeits the match.
normal.cn: 不出场的球队会被判弃权。

normal.en: A deposit is forfeited when the contract is broken.
normal.cn: 违约时押金会被没收。

normal.en: The noun forfeit names the penalty, as in pay a forfeit.
normal.cn: 名词 forfeit 指罚金，如「pay a forfeit」就是缴纳罚金。

normal.en: Forfeiture is the formal noun for the loss of a right.
normal.cn: forfeiture 是表示「权利丧失」的正式名词。

normal.en: Compare lose: forfeit always adds a rule or a penalty.
normal.cn: 对比 lose：forfeit 总带有规则或惩罚的意味。

abstract.en: See a referee lift the trophy away from a player.
abstract.cn: 想象裁判把奖杯从球员手里拿走。

abstract.en: See a form left blank and a place in the final quietly erased.
abstract.cn: 想象一张表格空着，决赛名额被悄悄划掉。

abstract.en: See coins dropped into a penalty box.
abstract.cn: 想象硬币被投进罚款箱。

examples.en: The club forfeited its licence after repeated safety failures.
examples.cn: 因多次安全违规，俱乐部被吊销了执照。

examples.en: She would rather forfeit the prize than break the rules.
examples.cn: 她宁可不要奖品，也不愿违反规则。

examples.en: A forfeit of fifty pounds is charged for late payment.
examples.cn: 逾期付款要缴五十英镑罚金。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「罚费特」——犯规之后被罚掉的一笔费用；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 foris（外面）+ facere（做）→ forisfacere（在法度之外行事）→ 古法语 forfait（罪行；罚没）→ 英语 forfeit，核心义「因越界而被拿走」。

sensesIntro.en: Forfeit starts as a loss ordered by law, widens to any loss that follows a wrong, then names the penalty and the thing taken, and finally covers sport and party games.
sensesIntro.cn: forfeit 先指法律判定的丧失，再扩大到任何因过错而来的损失，接着指罚金与被罚没之物，最后进入体育与派对游戏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a referee lifting the ball away from the player who broke the rule.
core.cn: 核心意象：裁判从违规球员那里把球拿走。

branches.en: Legal loss of property is the starting sense.
branches.cn: 依法丧失财产是起点义项。

branches.en: Loss caused by a wrong act and loss caused by a missed condition follow the same pattern.
branches.cn: 因过错而失去与因错过条件而失权走的是同一模式。

branches.en: The noun names both the penalty paid and the pledge kept.
branches.cn: 名词义既指缴纳的罚金，也指被扣下的抵押物。

branches.en: Total punishment takes life or freedom.
branches.cn: 最重的惩罚拿走生命或自由。

branches.en: Sport and party games turn the penalty into a result or a joke.
branches.cn: 体育与派对游戏把惩罚变成赛果或玩笑。

intro.en: Forfeit is built from Latin foris and facere, and English has added forfeiture and forfeitable around it.
intro.cn: forfeit 由拉丁语 foris 与 facere 构成，英语围绕它构成了 forfeiture 与 forfeitable。

latinIntro.en: Latin foris means outside, facere means to do, and forisfacere means to act outside the law.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 foris 意为「外面」，facere 意为「做」，forisfacere 意为「在法度之外行事」。

items.example: The prefix for- in forfeit comes from foris.
items.exampleCN: forfeit 中的前缀 for- 来自 foris。

items.example: Foris supplies the idea of stepping outside.
items.exampleCN: foris 提供「走到外面」的意思。

items.example: Facere is the source of the second half.
items.exampleCN: facere 是这个词后半部分的来源。
forisfacere 是它的法律词源。

items.example: Forfait carries the word into French.
items.exampleCN: forfait 把这个词带入法语。
forfeit 保留了法律含义。

items.meaning: the loss of a right or property
items.exampleCN: forfeiture 是正式名词。
后缀 -ure 构成 forfeiture。
forfeitable 描述可能被罚没的财产。
后缀 -able 构成 forfeitable。

可被罚没的
不丧失权益

definition_zh: 宽恕；原谅；饶恕；豁免
definition_en: the act of pardoning a wrong, or the state of being pardoned
core_image: 紧握的拳头慢慢松开，一张欠条被撕成两半
scene: 争吵过后，年长的一方先伸出手，把旧账翻了过去。After the quarrel, the older woman offered forgiveness and shook hands.
sceneCN: 这里 forgiveness 是「原谅、宽恕」（第 1 个义项：原谅他人的过错）；句意：争吵过后，年长的一方主动提出原谅，并与对方握手。

pos.zh: 宽恕；原谅；豁免

derivatives.zh: forgive 加 -ing 构成，形容「愿意原谅的、宽容的」
forgive 加 -able 构成，指「可原谅的」
un- 加 forgivable 构成，指「不可原谅的」
un- 加 forgiving 构成，指「不宽容的」

senses.title: The act of pardoning a wrong
senses.definition: the act of deciding not to punish or blame someone for something wrong
senses.definitionCN: 决定不因某人的过错而惩罚或责备对方的行为
senses.example: She asked for forgiveness after the quarrel.
senses.exampleCN: 争吵之后，她请求原谅。
senses.why: The Old English verb meant to give away, so forgiveness is the giving away of a claim against someone.
senses.whyCN: 古英语动词意为「给出去」，所以宽恕就是把对他人的追究交出去。

senses.title: The state of having been pardoned
senses.definition: the condition of having been pardoned, so that blame no longer rests on someone
senses.definitionCN: 已经获得原谅、责备不再落在此人身上的状态
senses.example: He lived in the relief that forgiveness brought.
senses.exampleCN: 他生活在宽恕带来的那份轻松里。
senses.why: The suffix -ness turns the act into a state, and a person can remain inside that state.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ness 把行为变成状态，人可以一直待在这个状态里。

senses.title: The willingness to release resentment
senses.definition: a disposition to let go of anger and resentment toward someone who has done wrong
senses.definitionCN: 对做错事的人放下愤怒与怨恨的心性
senses.example: Forgiveness is a choice before it is a feeling.
senses.exampleCN: 宽恕先是一种选择，然后才是一种感受。
senses.why: The same core image becomes a habit of the heart: the grip is released again and again.
senses.whyCN: 同一个核心意象变成心里的习惯：那只手一次又一次地松开。

senses.title: Mercy shown by a person in power
senses.definition: mercy or clemency shown by someone who has the power to punish
senses.definitionCN: 有惩罚权的人所表现出的仁慈或宽大
senses.example: The king granted forgiveness to the rebels.
senses.exampleCN: 国王赦免了叛乱者。
senses.why: When the person holding the penalty lets it go, the private release becomes official mercy.
senses.whyCN: 当握有惩罚权的人放手，私人的释怀就变成正式的宽赦。

senses.title: Religious pardon of sins
senses.definition: the divine pardon of sins, or the act of declaring that pardon
senses.definitionCN: 神对罪过的赦免，或宣布这种赦免的行为
senses.example: The prayer asks for forgiveness of sins.
senses.exampleCN: 这祈祷文祈求赦免罪过。
senses.why: Religious language makes the release total: the debt of sin is cancelled rather than postponed.
senses.whyCN: 宗教语言让释放变得彻底：罪债是被勾销，而不是被延期。

senses.title: Cancellation of a debt
senses.definition: the cancellation of a debt or a financial obligation
senses.definitionCN: 对债务或财务义务的取消
senses.example: The bank announced forgiveness of loans to farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 银行宣布豁免农民的贷款。
senses.why: Money owed is treated like a wrong owed: the record is wiped clean.
senses.whyCN: 欠下的钱被当作欠下的过错处理：记录被擦干净。

senses.title: Release from personal guilt
senses.definition: the process of releasing oneself from guilt over a past act
senses.definitionCN: 把自己从过去某件事的负罪感中释放出来的过程
senses.example: He practiced self-forgiveness after the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 事故之后，他练习自我原谅。
senses.why: The pardoned person can be the same person who did the wrong, so the releasing turns inward.
senses.whyCN: 被宽恕的人也可能正是做错事的人，于是释放转向内心。

senses.title: Remission of a punishment
senses.definition: the reduction or removal of a punishment that was already imposed
senses.definitionCN: 对已经施加的惩罚予以减轻或取消
senses.example: The court showed forgiveness by cutting the sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 法院缩短了刑期，显示出宽赦。
senses.why: The core image reaches the sentence itself: part of the penalty is lifted.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象一直延伸到判决本身：惩罚的一部分被拿掉了。

intro.en: Forgiveness comes from Old English forgiefan, to give away or pardon, a Germanic compound of for- and giefan, to give, plus the noun suffix -ness.
intro.cn: forgiveness 来自古英语 forgiefan（给出去、原谅），是 for- 与 giefan（给）构成的日耳曼语复合词，再加名词后缀 -ness。

items.en: A reconstructed Germanic compound of for- and give lies behind English forgive and German vergeben; the exact form is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 forgive 与德语 vergeben 背后是一个由 for- 与「给」构成的日耳曼语复合词，其确切形式已不可考。

items.en: Forgiefan means to grant, give away, or pardon.
items.cn: forgiefan 意为准予、给出去或原谅。

items.en: Forgifnes already names pardon as a state or quality.
items.cn: forgifnes 已经作为状态或性质指「赦免」。

items.en: Forgivenesse settles as the usual spelling of the noun.
items.cn: forgivenesse 逐渐固定为该名词的通常拼写。

items.en: The word extends from divine pardon to mercy between people.
items.cn: 这个词从神的赦免扩展到人与人之间的宽恕。

items.en: Psychology and finance add self-forgiveness and debt forgiveness.
items.cn: 心理学与金融领域增加了自我原谅与债务豁免的用法。

note.en: Forgiveness belongs to the forgive family, and its neighbours are words for pardon, mercy, and absolution.
note.cn: forgiveness 属于 forgive 词族，近邻则是表示赦免、仁慈与宽赦的词。

entries.definition: to stop blaming or punishing someone

normalIntro.en: Forgiveness is the moment a grip opens: a debt is torn up instead of collected.

normal.en: Forgive and forgiveness share one family: the verb names the act, the noun names the state.

normal.en: Ask for forgiveness after a quarrel, and grant forgiveness when the other person is ready.
normal.cn: 争吵之后请求原谅，等对方准备好时给予宽恕。

normal.en: Debt forgiveness cancels money owed, just as pardon cancels blame.
normal.cn: 债务豁免取消欠款，正如赦免取消责备。

normal.en: Self-forgiveness applies the same release to your own past mistakes.
normal.cn: 自我原谅把同样的释放用在自己过去的错误上。

normal.en: Compare pardon: pardon is often official, while forgiveness is usually personal.
normal.cn: 对比 pardon：pardon 常是官方的，forgiveness 通常是个人之间的。

abstract.en: See a fist slowly open and a crumpled receipt fall out.
abstract.cn: 想象一只拳头慢慢张开，一张皱巴巴的收据掉了出来。

abstract.en: See a written debt crossed out with one stroke.
abstract.cn: 想象一笔写下的欠款被一笔划掉。

abstract.en: See a heavy bag set down at a door and left behind.
abstract.cn: 想象一只沉重的袋子被放在门口，不再带走。

examples.cn: 他去找哥哥请求原谅。

examples.cn: 宽恕并不意味着伤害被遗忘。

sensesIntro.cn: forgiveness 从原谅的行为，走到被原谅的状态与放下怨恨的心性，再扩展到官方、宗教、金钱与内心的各种释放。

core.cn: 核心意象：紧握的拳头张开，欠条被撕成两半。

branches.en: The act of pardoning is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 原谅的行为是日常义项。

branches.en: Being pardoned and being willing to pardon are the state and the disposition.
branches.cn: 被原谅与愿意原谅分别是状态与心性。

branches.en: Official and religious pardon make the release formal.
branches.cn: 官方与宗教的赦免让释放变得正式。

branches.en: Debt relief and remission of punishment cancel what is owed.
branches.cn: 债务豁免与刑罚免除都取消所欠之物。

branches.en: The inward turn applies the release to oneself.
branches.cn: 转向内心的用法把释放施加于自身。

definition_en: to give up something pleasant, valuable, or expected, usually voluntarily
core_image: 筷子已经伸向那盘菜，又收回来，把菜留给别人
scene: 为了攒钱交学费，她把每天一杯的奶茶戒掉了。To save for tuition, she chose to forgo her daily milk tea.
sceneCN: 这里 forgo 是「戒掉、放弃（享受）」（第 1 个义项：自愿放弃某种享受）；句意：为了攒钱交学费，她选择放弃每天一杯奶茶。

pos.zh: 放弃；舍弃；戒除

derivatives.zh: forgo 加 -ing 构成名词，指「放弃、戒除」这一行为
forgo 的过去分词作形容词，指「已放弃的、已经成为过去的」

senses.title: To give up a pleasure on purpose
senses.definition: to decide not to have something enjoyable, often for a better reason
senses.definitionCN: 为了更好的理由而决定不要某种享受
senses.example: She forgoes coffee after noon so that she can sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 她过午不再喝咖啡，以便晚上能睡着。
senses.why: The Old English verb meant to go away from something, so the pleasure is left behind like a road not taken.
senses.whyCN: 古英语动词意为「从某物走开」，于是享受就像一条没走的路被留在身后。

senses.title: To abstain from something by rule
senses.definition: to keep away from food, drink, or pleasure as a matter of discipline, health, or faith
senses.definitionCN: 出于自律、健康或信仰而远离某些饮食或享乐
senses.example: The order forgoes meat during Lent.
senses.exampleCN: 该修会在四旬期内不吃肉。
senses.why: Going without becomes a repeated practice, and the single act turns into a rule of life.
senses.whyCN: 「不要」变成反复的实践，单次行为就成了生活规矩。

senses.title: To turn down an opportunity
senses.definition: to refuse an opportunity or advantage that one could have taken
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝本可抓住的机会或好处
senses.example: He forwent the promotion in order to stay in the same city.
senses.exampleCN: 为了留在同一座城市，他放弃了升职。
senses.why: An opportunity is something offered, so forgo means letting the offer pass without taking it.
senses.whyCN: 机会是别人递来的东西，forgo 就是让这份递来的东西过去而不接。

senses.title: To give up a legal claim
senses.definition: to surrender a right, title, or claim instead of insisting on it
senses.definitionCN: 不再坚持，从而交出权利、所有权或要求
senses.example: The family agreed to forgo its claim to the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人同意放弃对遗产的请求权。
senses.why: The core image applies to law: a claim is held in the hand and then the hand opens.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象用在法律上：请求权原本握在手里，然后手松开了。

senses.title: To do without what is scarce
senses.definition: to live or continue without something that is needed or expected
senses.definitionCN: 在缺少必需或应有之物的情况下继续生活
senses.example: The villagers had to forgo clean water for three days.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们有三天不得不将就没有干净水的日子。
senses.why: When the thing is not offered but simply absent, forgo names the plain fact of going on without it.
senses.whyCN: 当某物不是被拒绝而是根本缺席，forgo 就指「没有它也照常过下去」这一事实。

senses.title: To set aside a plan
senses.definition: to abandon a plan or intention, often for a larger purpose
senses.definitionCN: 放弃某个计划或打算，常是为了更大的目标
senses.example: The council forwent the new road to protect the wetland.
senses.exampleCN: 为保护湿地，议会放弃了修建新路的计划。
senses.why: A plan is a path one means to walk, so forgo means choosing not to set out on it.
senses.whyCN: 计划是一条打算走的路，forgo 就是选择不踏上这条路。

senses.title: To quit a habit for good
senses.definition: to stop a habitual pleasure or practice and not return to it
senses.definitionCN: 停止某种习惯性的享乐或做法，并且不再回到其中
senses.example: After the heart attack, he forwent tobacco for good.
senses.exampleCN: 心脏病发作之后，他彻底戒了烟。
senses.why: The word can mark a final departure: the road back is closed, not merely postponed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以表示最终的离开：回头的路被关上，而不只是推迟。

senses.title: To trade a gain for a larger good
senses.definition: to accept the loss of a benefit in order to gain something more important
senses.definitionCN: 为了换取更重要的东西而接受某项好处的损失
senses.example: The firm forwent short-term profit to keep its reputation.
senses.exampleCN: 公司舍弃短期利润，以保住声誉。
senses.why: The core image becomes a trade: the thing released is weighed against a greater good.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象变成一种交换：放掉的东西要跟更大的好处放在一起权衡。

intro.en: Forgo comes from Old English forgan, to go without, from for-, away or beyond, and gan, to go; the variant forego also means to precede.
intro.cn: forgo 来自古英语 forgan（不去、戒除），由 for-（离开、越过）与 gan（走）构成；异体 forego 另有「先行、在前」之义。

items.en: A Germanic prefix meaning away or beyond combines with the verb go; the exact reconstructed form is uncertain, and German vergehen is a parallel.
items.cn: 一个表示「离开、越过」的日耳曼语前缀与动词「走」结合；确切的重构形式存疑，德语 vergehen 是平行例子。

items.en: Forgān means to go past, go without, or abstain.
items.cn: forgān 意为走过、没有……而过或戒除。

items.en: Forgon keeps the sense of doing without.
items.cn: forgon 保留了「没有……也行」的意思。

items.en: Forgo and forego are both used, and forego also means to go before.
items.cn: forgo 与 forego 两种拼写都在使用，而 forego 还表示「走在前面」。

items.en: Forgo settles as the spelling for doing without, common in formal writing.
items.cn: forgo 固定为表示「没有……也行」的拼写，常见于正式书面语。

note.en: Forgo is the verb of going without; its family includes forgoing and forgone, and its neighbours are words for abstaining and relinquishing.
note.cn: forgo 是表示「没有……也行」的动词，同族词包括 forgoing 与 forgone，近邻则是表示戒除与交出的词。

senses.title: The quality of being formal
senses.definition: the quality of being serious, polite, and correct according to accepted rules or custom
senses.definitionCN: 严肃、有礼、合乎既定规矩的性质
senses.example: The formality of the hall made the visitors lower their voices.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅的庄重气氛让来访者放低了声音。
senses.why: The word is built on formal, from Latin forma, a shape; behaving with formality means acting according to a set pattern.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 formal 派生，formal 来自拉丁语 forma（形状）；讲 formality 就是照着既定「形状」行事。

senses.title: Stiff or ceremonial manner
senses.definition: stiffness or excessive ceremony in the way someone behaves
senses.definitionCN: 举止中过分的拘谨或繁文缛节
senses.example: His formality vanished as soon as the guests left.
senses.exampleCN: 客人一走，他的拘谨就消失了。
senses.why: When the pattern is followed too tightly, the manner itself turns stiff, and the word comes to name that stiffness.
senses.whyCN: 规矩跟得太紧，举止本身就会变僵，于是这个词也指这种僵硬。

senses.title: An official procedure
senses.definition: an official act or step that has to be completed before something can be done
senses.definitionCN: 办成某事之前必须完成的官方步骤
senses.example: The formalities at the border took nearly an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 边境的手续花了将近一个小时。
senses.why: The abstract quality turns into concrete steps: every form that must be filled in is a formality.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的性质落成一道道具体步骤：每一张必须填的表都是 formality。

senses.title: A mere formality
senses.definition: something done only because rule or custom demands it, with no real effect on the result
senses.definitionCN: 只因规定或习俗而做、对结果并无实际影响的事
senses.example: The safety check was a mere formality before the race.
senses.exampleCN: 赛前的安全检查只是走个形式。
senses.why: When the outward pattern survives but the substance has gone, the act becomes an empty shell.
senses.whyCN: 外在形式还在、实质已经空了，这个行为就只剩一层壳。

senses.title: The degree of formal style
senses.titleCN: 正式程度；文体的正式性
senses.definition: the extent to which language or style follows formal conventions rather than casual ones
senses.definitionCN: 语言或文体遵循正式规范而非随意表达的程度
senses.example: Academic writing requires a higher level of formality than a chat.
senses.exampleCN: 学术写作比闲聊需要更高的正式程度。
senses.why: The general quality can be measured, so formality also names a scale from casual to highly formal.
senses.whyCN: 这种性质可以度量，于是 formality 也指从随意到极正式的等级刻度。

intro.en: Formality comes from Latin forma, a shape or pattern, through formalis and formalitas, and then Old French formalité.
intro.cn: formality 源自拉丁语 forma（形状、模型），经 formalis 与 formalitas，再由古法语 formalité 进入英语。

items.en: Forma means a shape, a mould, or a pattern.
items.cn: forma 意为形状、模子或样式。

items.en: Formalis means belonging to a form or pattern.
items.cn: formalis 意为属于形式或样式的。

items.en: Formalitas names the quality of having a form.
items.cn: formalitas 指具有形式的性质。

items.en: Formalité carries the word into French as a ceremonial observance.
items.cn: formalité 把词带进法语，指礼节上的讲究。

items.en: Formality first names a customary or legal observance in English.
items.cn: formality 最初在英语中指习俗或法律上的正式做法。

items.en: Modern English adds the sense of stiff manner and of a level of formal style.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了拘谨举止与正式程度这两个义项。

note.en: Formality is the noun of formal, with a large word family and close ties to words for ceremony and procedure.
note.cn: formality 是 formal 的名词，词族很大，并与仪式、程序类词相邻。

entries.definition: following accepted rules; official
entries.definitionCN: 正式的；合乎既定规矩的

entries.definition: to make something official or fixed in form
entries.definitionCN: 使正式化；使定形

entries.definition: too much attention to outward form
entries.definitionCN: 形式主义；过分看重外在形式

entries.definition: a formal public act or event
entries.definitionCN: 典礼；仪式

entries.definition: the accepted rules of formal behaviour
entries.definitionCN: 礼节；外交礼仪

entries.definition: the rules of polite behaviour in a group
entries.definitionCN: 礼仪；规矩

normalIntro.en: Formality belongs to the family of formal: Latin forma, a shape, is the picture behind every rule of ceremony.
normalIntro.cn: formality 属于 formal 一族：拉丁语 forma（形状）就是一切礼节规矩背后的画面。

normal.en: Formal and formality share the root forma, a shape: to act with formality is to fit a set shape.
normal.cn: formal 与 formality 共用词根 forma（形状）：按形式办事，就是套进既定形状。

normal.en: Formalities are the steps themselves, such as papers and stamps at a border.
normal.cn: formalities 指一道道步骤，比如边境处的表格与盖章。

normal.en: A mere formality is done for the rule only, with no real effect.
normal.cn: 「a mere formality」只为规矩而做，没有实际影响。

normal.en: With great formality means with full ceremony and seriousness.
normal.cn: 「with great formality」表示以十足的礼节与郑重。

normal.en: Compare ceremony: a ceremony is the event, while formality stresses the rules that surround it.
normal.cn: 对比 ceremony：ceremony 是仪式本身，formality 更强调围绕仪式的规矩。

abstract.en: Picture a hall with a red carpet and everyone standing in a fixed order.
abstract.cn: 想象一间铺红毯的大厅，所有人按固定次序站好。

abstract.en: Picture a man buttoning his collar right up to the top.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把衣领一直扣到最上面。

abstract.en: Picture a counter where each form gets one more stamp.
abstract.cn: 想象柜台前，每张表格都要再盖一个章。

examples.en: The formalities at the border took nearly an hour.
examples.cn: 边境的手续花了将近一个小时。

examples.en: She treated the interview as a mere formality.
examples.cn: 她把面试只当作走个形式。

examples.en: A little formality can help strangers work together.
examples.cn: 一点正式的礼节能帮助陌生人合作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛么理体」——办事讲理、讲体面，处处照规矩，这就是 formality 的正式与礼节；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 forma（形状、模型）→ formalis（属于形式的）→ formalitas（形式性）→ 古法语 formalité → 英语 formality；核心义是「照既定的形状办事」，故有正式、手续、拘谨等义。

sensesIntro.en: Formality starts as the quality of following a set form, then names stiff ceremony, the official steps themselves, the empty shell of a form, and finally a measurable level of formal style.
sensesIntro.cn: formality 从「照着既定形式行事」这一性质出发，继而指拘谨的礼节、具体手续、只剩外壳的形式，最后指可度量的正式程度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: every button fastened, every step following the pattern.
core.cn: 核心意象：扣好每一颗扣子，每一步都照规矩来。

branches.en: The general quality of being formal is the base sense.
branches.cn: 讲正式、郑重是基础义项。

branches.en: Stiff ceremony is the same quality hardened into manner.
branches.cn: 拘谨的礼节是同一性质僵化成的举止。

branches.en: Official steps are the quality turned into concrete acts.
branches.cn: 正式手续是这一性质落成的具体行为。

branches.en: An empty form keeps the act but loses the substance.
branches.cn: 空有形式保留了行为，却丢掉了实质。

branches.en: A measurable level of style grows out of the general quality.
branches.cn: 可度量的文体等级从这种一般性质中长出。

intro.en: Formality is built from the Latin noun forma and the suffixes -alis, -itas, and English -ity, with formal, formalize, and formalism around it.
intro.cn: formality 由拉丁语名词 forma 与后缀 -alis、-itas 以及英语后缀 -ity 构成，周围有 formal、formalize 与 formalism。

latinIntro.en: Latin forma means shape; formalis means of a form, and formalitas means the quality of a form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 forma 意为形状；formalis 意为形式的，formalitas 意为形式的性质。

items.example: Forma is the shape behind the word.
items.exampleCN: forma 是这个词背后的「形状」。
后缀 -alis 构成 formalis。

items.example: Formalis links the noun to the quality.
items.exampleCN: formalis 把名词与性质连起来。
后缀 -itas 构成 formalitas。

items.example: Formalitas passes into French and English.
items.exampleCN: formalitas 传入法语与英语。

items.example: Formal is the adjective of formality.
items.exampleCN: formal 是 formality 的形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ity turns formal into formality.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 把 formal 变成 formality。
formality 保留名词含义。
formalize 加了动词后缀 -ize。
formalism 加了名词后缀 -ism。

definition_zh: 令人敬畏的；强大的；艰巨的；难以对付的；数量惊人的
definition_en: causing fear or respect because of great size, strength, or difficulty
core_image: 一座高墙立在眼前，抬头看不到顶，风从墙头压下来
scene: 球场的看台上有人低声说，对面那支队伍今年不好惹。On the pitch, the visiting side looked formidable from the first whistle.
sceneCN: 这里 formidable 是「强大得令人敬畏」（第 2 个义项：实力强到让对手心生敬畏）；句意：开场哨一响，客队就显得气势逼人。

pos.zh: 令人敬畏的；强大的；艰巨的；难以对付的；数量惊人的

senses.title: Causing fear or awe
senses.titleCN: 令人畏惧的；令人敬畏的
senses.definition: so impressive or alarming that it makes people feel fear or deep respect
senses.definitionCN: 气势逼人，使人害怕或心生深深的敬意
senses.example: The old fortress was formidable even in ruins.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧堡垒即使成了废墟，依然气势逼人。
senses.why: Latin formido is fear itself, and formidabilis names whatever brings that fear.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 formido 就是恐惧，formidabilis 指带来恐惧的东西。

senses.title: Very strong or powerful
senses.definition: having great strength, skill, or resources, so that opposing it is hard
senses.definitionCN: 力量、技艺或资源很强，难以与之抗衡
senses.example: The champion built a formidable defence that season.
senses.exampleCN: 那位冠军在那个赛季打造出强大的防线。
senses.why: Fear shades into plain respect for power, so the word praises strength as well as warning of it.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧淡化为对力量的纯粹敬意，于是这个词既示警也称赞。

senses.title: Very difficult to deal with
senses.definition: presenting great difficulty, so that handling it takes unusual effort or skill
senses.definitionCN: 难度很大，处理起来需要格外的努力或本领
senses.example: Rebuilding the bridge was a formidable task.
senses.exampleCN: 重建这座桥是一项艰巨的任务。
senses.why: A task that resists you feels like an opponent too strong to push aside.
senses.whyCN: 一件顶着你的难事，也像推不开的强敌。

senses.title: Very large in amount or scale
senses.definition: large enough in size or number to alarm or overwhelm
senses.definitionCN: 规模或数量大到令人心惊、难以应付
senses.example: The inquiry faced a formidable stack of documents.
senses.exampleCN: 调查组面对的是堆积如山的文件。
senses.why: Sheer size produces the same awe as strength, so the adjective extends to quantity.
senses.whyCN: 单纯的大也会带来与力量相同的敬畏，于是这个词延伸指数量。

senses.title: Commanding admiration through excellence
senses.definition: so impressive in ability or quality that it wins admiration and respect
senses.definitionCN: 能力或品质出众到令人敬佩
senses.example: She has a formidable command of three languages.
senses.exampleCN: 她精通三种语言，令人叹服。
senses.why: When the fear fades completely, what remains is admiration for something far above the ordinary.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧完全退去后，剩下的是对远超寻常之物的敬佩。

intro.en: Formidable comes straight from Latin formidabilis, causing fear, from formidare, to dread, and formido, fear.
intro.cn: formidable 直接来自拉丁语 formidabilis（令人恐惧的），源于 formidare（畏惧）与 formido（恐惧）。

items.en: Formido means fear or dread.
items.cn: formido 意为恐惧、惊骇。

items.en: Formidare means to fear or to dread.
items.cn: formidare 意为畏惧。

items.en: Formidabilis means causing fear.
items.cn: formidabilis 意为令人恐惧的。

items.en: Middle French adopts formidable with the sense that causes dread.
items.cn: 中古法语借入 formidable，保留令人畏惧之义。

items.en: English uses formidable for what is fearsome or hard to oppose.
items.cn: 英语用 formidable 形容可怕或难以对抗的事物。

items.en: The sense softens toward impressively strong, difficult, or large.
items.cn: 词义软化为「强得惊人、难得惊人、大得惊人」。

note.en: Formidable belongs to a small Latin family of fear words, and it is close to several adjectives of difficulty and threat.
note.cn: formidable 属于拉丁语「恐惧」小词族，与一批表示艰难、威胁的形容词相邻。

entries.definition: in a fearsome or impressively strong way
entries.definitionCN: 令人敬畏地；以强大气势

entries.definition: the quality of being fearsome or hard to deal with
entries.definitionCN: 可畏；难以对付的性质

entries.definition: shape or appearance
entries.definitionCN: 形状；形式（只是拼写相近，词源不同：form 来自拉丁语 forma，formidable 来自 formido「恐惧」）

entries.definition: causing fear
entries.definitionCN: 可怕的；吓人的

entries.definition: making someone feel worried about their ability to succeed
entries.definitionCN: 令人望而生畏的；使人气馁的

entries.definition: making people feel frightened or less confident
entries.definitionCN: 令人发怵的；使人不自信的

normalIntro.en: Formidable carries Latin fear in its first syllable, and that fear has softened into respect.
normalIntro.cn: formidable 的第一截藏着拉丁语的「恐惧」，这份恐惧后来软化成敬意。

normal.en: Formido is Latin for fear, and formidable describes what produces it.
normal.cn: formido 在拉丁语中意为恐惧，formidable 就形容引起恐惧之物。

normal.en: A formidable opponent is one you respect before the match starts.
normal.cn: 「a formidable opponent」是比赛未开始就让你心生敬意的对手。

normal.en: A formidable task is one that makes you take a deep breath.
normal.cn: 「a formidable task」是让你先深吸一口气的任务。

normal.en: The adverb is formidably, as in a formidably complex system.
normal.cn: 副词形式是 formidably，例如「a formidably complex system」（复杂得惊人）。

normal.en: Compare fearsome: fearsome only frightens, while formidable also carries respect.
normal.cn: 对比 fearsome：fearsome 只是吓人，formidable 还带着敬意。

abstract.en: Picture a wall so high that the top disappears into cloud.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵高墙，墙顶没入云里。

abstract.en: Picture a line of very tall players walking onto the pitch.
abstract.cn: 想象一排高大的球员走进球场。

abstract.en: Picture a desk buried under folders that still keeps growing.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子被文件夹埋住，还越堆越高。

examples.en: The mountain presents a formidable climb for beginners.
examples.cn: 这座山对新手来说是一段艰巨的攀登。

examples.en: Their defence proved formidable in the second half.
examples.cn: 他们的防线在下半场显得难以攻破。

examples.en: Clearing the old factory site was a formidable challenge.
examples.cn: 清理旧厂址是一项巨大的挑战。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛弥得宝」——佛像高大得让人仰头，宝物藏在高处，看着就令人生畏；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 formido（恐惧）→ formidare（畏惧）→ formidabilis（令人恐惧的）→ 法语 formidable → 英语 formidable；核心义由「可怕」软化为「强大得令人敬畏」。

sensesIntro.en: Formidable moves from plain fear, through sheer power, difficulty, and size, to admiration.
sensesIntro.cn: formidable 从纯粹的恐惧出发，经力量、难度与规模，最后落到敬佩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall so high that its top is lost in cloud.
core.cn: 核心意象：一堵高得望不见顶的墙。

branches.en: Awe tinged with fear is the root sense.
branches.cn: 带恐惧的敬畏是根源义项。

branches.en: Strength that makes opposition hard is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 强到难以抗衡的力量是日常义项。

branches.en: Difficulty borrows the image of an unbeatable opponent.
branches.cn: 难度借用了「打不败的对手」这一意象。

branches.en: Great size produces awe without any threat.
branches.cn: 巨大的规模不带威胁，也同样令人心惊。

branches.en: Admiration is fear refined into respect.
branches.cn: 敬佩是恐惧提炼后的敬意。

intro.cn: formidable 建在拉丁语 formido（恐惧）之上，带形容词后缀 -abilis 与其英语对应形式 -able。

latinIntro.en: Latin formido means fear; formidare means to dread, and formidabilis means causing fear.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 formido 意为恐惧；formidare 意为畏惧，formidabilis 意为令人恐惧的。

items.exampleCN: formido 提供恐惧的核心。

items.example: Formidare is the verb of fearing.
items.exampleCN: formidare 是表示畏惧的动词。
formidabilis 是直接来源。
后缀 -abilis 构成这个形容词。
英语 -able 与拉丁后缀呼应。

items.meaningCN: 令人敬畏的；强大得惊人的
items.exampleCN: formidable 保留形容词身份。
后缀 -ly 构成 formidably。

items.example: The suffix -ly turns adjectives into adverbs.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 把形容词变成副词。

definition_zh: 即将发生的；即将出版的；乐于提供信息的；可得到的
definition_en: going to happen or appear soon, or willing to give information
core_image: 海边的桅杆先升出海平线，船身还没出现，正朝岸边来
scene: 会议室的墙上贴着下一季的日程，第一场活动的时间已经印好。The first of the forthcoming events is a public lecture in May.
sceneCN: 这里 forthcoming 是「即将举行的」（第 1 个义项：事情即将发生）；句意：接下来那些活动里，第一场是五月的公开讲座。

pos.zh: 即将发生的；即将出版的；乐于提供信息的；可得到的

derivatives.zh: 坦率；乐于提供信息；在 forthcoming 上加 -ness 构成，指乐于开口的性质

senses.title: About to happen
senses.titleCN: 即将发生的；即将举行的
senses.definition: going to happen or take place very soon
senses.definitionCN: 很快就要发生或举行
senses.example: The forthcoming election has dominated the news.
senses.exampleCN: 即将举行的选举占据了新闻头条。
senses.why: Forth means forward and coming means arriving, so what is forthcoming is coming forward toward the present.
senses.whyCN: forth 意为向前，coming 意为到来；forthcoming 就是正向现在走来。

senses.title: About to be published or released
senses.definition: due to appear in print, on screen, or on sale within a short time
senses.definitionCN: 短期内即将付印、上映或上市
senses.example: Her forthcoming novel is already being adapted for television.
senses.exampleCN: 她即将出版的小说已经在改编成电视剧。
senses.why: A book or film that comes forward into the market is announced before it arrives.
senses.whyCN: 书或电影在面世前先「向前走来」进入市场，于是有了这个义项。

senses.title: Willing to give information
senses.titleCN: 乐于提供信息的；坦诚的
senses.definition: open and willing to talk, especially about facts that others want to know
senses.definitionCN: 愿意开口，尤其愿意说出别人想知道的情况
senses.example: The minister was not forthcoming about the cost of the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 大臣不愿透露这项计划的成本。
senses.why: Someone who comes forward with words is open rather than closed, so the spatial image turns social.
senses.whyCN: 愿意「向前」把话说出来的人是不封闭的，空间意象就转成了人际态度。

senses.title: Available when needed
senses.definition: offered or provided readily, especially help, money, or a reply
senses.definitionCN: 在需要时能顺利得到或提供，尤指帮助、资金或答复
senses.example: No extra funding was forthcoming from the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 部里没有提供额外的资金。
senses.why: What comes forward can also be handed over, so the word covers whatever arrives when it is wanted.
senses.whyCN: 「向前而来」的东西也可以被交到手里，于是这个词也指需要时到手的东西。

intro.en: Forthcoming is a native English compound: forth, forward, plus coming, the participle of come.
intro.cn: forthcoming 是英语本土的合成词：forth（向前）加 coming（come 的分词）。

items.en: Forþ means forward or onward.
items.cn: forþ 意为向前、往前。

items.en: Cuman means to come, to arrive.
items.cn: cuman 意为来、到达。

items.en: Coming, the present participle, joins with forth.
items.cn: 现在分词 coming 与 forth 结合。

items.en: Forthcoming is recorded for what is about to appear.
items.cn: forthcoming 开始指即将出现的事物。

items.en: The sense of willing to give information appears later in the century.
items.cn: 「乐于提供信息」这一义项在同一个世纪稍后出现。

items.en: The word now covers events, publications, people, and funds.
items.cn: 如今这个词覆盖事件、出版物、人物与资金。

note.en: Forthcoming is a transparent compound, close in form to forth and coming and in meaning to words for what is soon or openly offered.
note.cn: forthcoming 是透明的合成词，形式上与 forth、coming 相邻，意义上与表示「即将」和「坦率提供」的词相邻。

entries.definition: forward in space or time
entries.definitionCN: 向前；往外（与 forthcoming 共用 forth 这一成分）

entries.definition: arriving or about to arrive
entries.definitionCN: 到来的；即将到来的（与 forthcoming 共用 coming）

entries.definition: the quality of being open or available
entries.definitionCN: 坦率；可得到

entries.definition: about to happen
entries.definitionCN: 即将发生的

entries.definition: about to happen very soon
entries.definitionCN: 迫在眉睫的

entries.definition: honest and direct in speech
entries.definitionCN: 坦率的；直言不讳的

normalIntro.en: Forthcoming is a picture word: something is coming forth, toward you, out of the future.
normalIntro.cn: forthcoming 是个画面词：有东西正从未来「向前」朝你走来。

normal.en: Forth is forward and coming is arriving, so forthcoming means coming toward the present.
normal.cn: forth 是向前，coming 是到来，所以 forthcoming 是朝现在走来。

normal.en: A forthcoming event is still ahead of you on the calendar.
normal.cn: 「a forthcoming event」是日程上还没到的那件事。

normal.en: A forthcoming book exists but has not reached the shops.
normal.cn: 「a forthcoming book」已经写好，却还没进书店。

normal.en: Be forthcoming about a problem means to talk about it openly.
normal.cn: 「be forthcoming about a problem」就是把问题摊开来说。

normal.en: Compare upcoming: upcoming only marks time, while forthcoming also covers openness and availability.
normal.cn: 对比 upcoming：upcoming 只标时间，forthcoming 还含坦诚与可得之意。

abstract.en: Picture a mast rising over the horizon before the hull appears.
abstract.cn: 想象船身还没出现，桅杆先升出海平线。

abstract.en: Picture a printing press rolling out a book that is not yet on sale.
abstract.cn: 想象印刷机刚印出一本还没上架的书。

abstract.en: Picture a colleague sliding a folder across the table without being asked.
abstract.cn: 想象同事没等你开口就把文件夹推过来。

examples.en: Details of the forthcoming trip will be posted online.
examples.cn: 即将到来的旅行的细节会发布在网上。

examples.en: The magazine is running a preview of her forthcoming book.
examples.cn: 这本杂志正在刊出她即将出版的新书预览。

examples.en: He was surprisingly forthcoming about his own mistakes.
examples.cn: 他出乎意料地坦诚谈起了自己的过失。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛寺康明」——庙里的钟声一响，好消息正朝你走来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 forþ（向前）+ cuman（来）→ coming（现在分词）→ 英语 forthcoming，字面「正向前而来」，故指即将到来、即将面世，也指人乐于开口、资源随手可得。

sensesIntro.en: Forthcoming begins with the literal picture of something coming forward, then marks what is about to happen or appear, then people and things that come forward when wanted.
sensesIntro.cn: forthcoming 从「有东西向前而来」这一字面画面出发，先指即将发生或面世，再指人和资源在需要时「走上前来」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mast rising over the horizon, the ship still out of sight.
core.cn: 核心意象：桅杆先升出海平线，船身还没出现。

branches.en: Coming toward the present gives the time sense.
branches.cn: 朝现在走来，给出时间义项。

branches.en: The same movement toward the market gives the publication sense.
branches.cn: 同样的「向市场走来」给出出版义项。

branches.en: Both a date and a title come forward before they arrive.
branches.cn: 日期与作品都在抵达之前先「向前」露面。

branches.en: A person who comes forward with words is open.
branches.cn: 愿意向前开口的人就是坦诚的。

branches.en: What comes forward can also be handed over when needed.
branches.cn: 向前而来的东西也能在需要时被交到手里。

intro.en: Forthcoming is a native compound of forth and coming; it has no Latin root, so the Latin family list stays empty.
intro.cn: forthcoming 是 forth 与 coming 的本土合成词，没有拉丁词根，因此拉丁同源词一栏留空。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor here: forth descends from Old English forþ, and coming from cuman, to come.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语祖先：forth 来自古英语 forþ，coming 来自 cuman（来）。

items.example: Forþ is the Old English spelling of forth.
items.exampleCN: forþ 是 forth 的古英语拼法。

items.example: Forth is the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: forth 是合成词的前半。

items.example: Cuman is the Old English verb of coming.
items.exampleCN: cuman 是表示「来」的古英语动词。
come 提供后半的意思。
后缀 -ing 构成 coming。

items.example: Coming is the participle of come.
items.exampleCN: coming 是 come 的分词。
forthcoming 把两半合起来。
后缀 -ness 构成 forthcomingness。
forthcomingness 指这种性质。

definition_zh: 直率的；坦白的；直截了当的；径直向前的
definition_en: direct and honest in speech, and clear in meaning, without trying to hide anything
core_image: 一条笔直的路，说话人沿着它直走到听者面前，一次也不拐弯
scene: 会议上，她没有绕弯子，直接把问题摆到桌面。Her forthright reply surprised everyone in the room.
sceneCN: 这里 forthright 是「直率坦白的」（第 1 个义项：说话直接、不掩饰）；句意：她直率的回答让屋里所有人都吃了一惊。

pos.zh: 直率的；坦白的；直截了当的
（古）径直地；立即

derivatives.zh: 直率地；坦率地（forthright 加副词词尾 -ly）
直率；坦白（forthright 加名词词尾 -ness，指这种品质）

senses.title: Direct and honest in speech
senses.definition: saying plainly what one thinks, even when the truth is uncomfortable
senses.definitionCN: 坦率地说出自己的想法，即使实情让人不舒服
senses.example: She gave a forthright account of the failure.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这次失败做了直率的说明。
senses.why: The Old English word pictured a straight road, so a forthright speaker goes straight to the point.
senses.whyCN: 古英语原词画的是一条直路，所以说话直的人总是直奔要点。

senses.title: Clear and unambiguous
senses.definition: expressed in a clear way that leaves no doubt about the meaning
senses.definitionCN: 表达清楚，不留下任何含义上的疑问
senses.example: The committee issued a forthright statement about the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会就延误发表了一份明确的声明。
senses.why: Straightness of movement became straightness of meaning, so a clear answer or refusal also earns the word.
senses.whyCN: 行走的「直」变成了意思的「直」，因此明确的回答或拒绝也能用这个词。

senses.title: Straight onward, at once
senses.definition: moving straight forward, or acting immediately, in older usage
senses.definitionCN: 径直向前，或立刻行动，属于较古老的用法
senses.example: In the old ballad the knight rides forthright to the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 在那首古老的歌谣里，骑士径直骑马来到门前。
senses.why: The original form was an adverb of direction, and the modern adjective grew out of that straight-line image.
senses.whyCN: 原形是指方向的副词，现代形容词正是从这条直线的意象里长出来的。

intro.en: Forthright is a native English compound of forth, forward, and right, straight.
intro.cn: forthright 是英语本土复合词，由 forth（向前）与 right（直、正）合成。

items.en: Forth means forward or onward, from a Germanic root.
items.cn: forth 意为向前、往前，源自日耳曼语词根。

items.en: Riht means straight or correct, and it is the ancestor of right.
items.cn: riht 意为直、正确，是 right 的前身。

items.en: Forthrihte is an adverb meaning straight on or immediately.
items.cn: forthrihte 是副词，意为径直向前或立刻。

items.en: The adverb also begins to describe a direct path or a plain manner.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，这个词也开始形容直接的路线或直白的方式。

items.en: Writers apply it to people and words that hide nothing.
items.cn: 十六、十七世纪的作者用它形容不藏掖的人和话。

items.en: The adjective is standard, while the adverb survives in older prose.
items.cn: 现代英语里形容词是标准用法，副词则多见于较旧的散文。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the forth or right shape; the near-meaning group runs from frank speech to blunt speech.
note.cn: 形近组共享 forth 或 right 的形状；近义组从坦率之言排到近乎生硬的直言。

entries.definition: Forward or onward, mainly in set phrases such as bring forth.
entries.definitionCN: 向前；往前，多用于 bring forth 一类固定短语，与 forthright 共享同一成分。

entries.definition: Complete and direct, with no qualification or delay.
entries.definitionCN: 完全的；直截了当的，同样由 right（直）构成，与 forthright 共享这一成分。

entries.definition: Standing vertically, and by extension honest in conduct.
entries.definitionCN: 直立的，引申为品行正直的；拼写里同样含 right（直）。

entries.definition: Open and honest in a friendly, relaxed way.
entries.definitionCN: 坦率的；友好的直言，语气比 forthright 温和。

entries.definition: Honest and direct, even about difficult or personal matters.
entries.definitionCN: 坦诚的；连难说的事也直说，常用于正式场合。

entries.definition: Direct to the point of seeming rude or tactless.
entries.definitionCN: 直截了当到近乎生硬的；缺乏委婉。

normalIntro.en: Forthright is forth plus right: move straight forward and speak straight.
normalIntro.cn: forthright 是 forth 加 right：一直向前走，也把话说直。

normal.en: Forth means forward, right means straight, so the word is a straight line.
normal.cn: forth 是向前，right 是直，这个词合起来就是一条直线。

normal.en: A forthright answer arrives without a cushion of polite hints.
normal.cn: forthright 的回答没有客套铺垫，直接到位。

normal.en: Forthrightness is the noun, and forthrightly is the adverb.
normal.cn: 名词是 forthrightness，副词是 forthrightly。

normal.en: Compare frank: frank is warmer, while forthright is firmer.
normal.cn: 对比 frank：frank 更温和，forthright 更坚定。

normal.en: Forthright people are valued in meetings but can upset sensitive listeners.
normal.cn: 直率的人在会议上受重视，却可能让敏感的人不舒服。

abstract.en: Picture a speaker walking a ruler-straight road to the listener.
abstract.cn: 想象说话的人沿一条尺子般笔直的路走到听者面前。

abstract.en: Think of an arrow that flies straight to the target of meaning.
abstract.cn: 想象一支箭笔直飞向「意思」这个靶心。

abstract.en: See a person stepping straight through an open door, never turning.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人径直穿过敞开的门，一次也不拐弯。

examples.en: He is forthright about the risks of the plan.
examples.cn: 他直言这个计划的风险。

examples.en: A forthright refusal is better than a vague promise.
examples.cn: 干脆的拒绝胜过含糊的承诺。

examples.en: Her forthright manner makes meetings shorter.
examples.cn: 她直率的作风让会议更短。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「佛莱特」——想象一位说话像尺子一样直的僧人；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 forth（向前）+ riht（直、正）→ forthrihte（径直向前）→ 中古英语 forthright，核心义「一直向前、不拐弯」。

sensesIntro.en: Forthright starts as a direction word, becomes a plain-speaking adjective, and keeps an older adverbial use at the edge.
sensesIntro.cn: forthright 最初是方向词，后来成为形容说话直白的形容词，古老的副词用法则留在边缘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight road from speaker to listener, with no bend.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条从说话人直通听者、没有弯折的路。

branches.en: Plain speech about people and choices.
branches.cn: 对人、对选择的直白说法。

branches.en: A clear statement, answer, or refusal.
branches.cn: 明确的声明、回答或拒绝。

branches.en: The old adverb of straight movement.
branches.cn: 表示径直移动的古老副词。

branches.en: Both senses remove the cushion of vague words.
branches.cn: 两个义项都抽掉了含糊措辞的垫子。

branches.en: Straightness of path and straightness of meaning share one image.
branches.cn: 路的直与意思的直共享同一个意象。

intro.en: Forthright is built from two native English pieces, forth and right, and the family grows with -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: forthright 由 forth 与 right 两个英语本土成分构成，词族靠 -ly 与 -ness 扩展。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor here; the two parts are Old English forth and riht.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖先，两个成分是古英语的 forth 与 riht。

items.exampleCN: forth 出现在「bring forth」中。

items.example: Riht is the ancestor of right.
items.exampleCN: riht 是 right 的前身。
right 保留了「直」的意象。
forthrightly 以 -ly 结尾。
forthrightness 表示这种品质。
她直率地回答。
他的直率赢得了信任。

items.example: Forthcoming is a cousin in meaning.
items.exampleCN: forthcoming 在意思上是近亲。
straightforward 在意思上与之重叠。

definition_zh: 加固；设防；强化；鼓舞
definition_en: to make something stronger, safer, or more effective, whether a structure, a food, or a person
core_image: 石匠往城墙的裂缝里填进新石块，墙体一层层变厚
scene: 暴雨来临前，村民们连夜给裂开的堤坝加筑石块。The volunteers worked until dawn to fortify the damaged embankment.
sceneCN: 这里 fortify 是「加固、使坚固」（第 1 个义项：把结构做得更结实）；句意：志愿者们一直干到天亮，加固受损的堤岸。

pos.zh: 加固；设防于；强化（营养）；鼓舞

derivatives.zh: 加固；防御工事；营养强化（fortify 加名词词尾 -fication）
加固者；强化剂（fortify 加表施动者的词尾 -er）
未设防的；未强化的（否定前缀 un- 加 fortified）

senses.title: Make a structure stronger
senses.definition: to make a building, wall, or structure stronger and harder to break
senses.definitionCN: 使建筑、墙体或结构更结实、更难被破坏
senses.example: Engineers fortified the sea wall with concrete.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师用混凝土加固了海堤。
senses.why: The Latin base fortis means strong, and the verb was first used for building works.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 fortis 意为「强」，这个动词最早正用于营造工程。

senses.title: Prepare a place for defence
senses.definition: to build defences around a town or position so that an enemy cannot take it
senses.definitionCN: 在城镇或阵地周围修筑防御，使敌人无法攻取
senses.example: The army fortified the hill before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 军队在黎明前给山头设防。
senses.why: Strengthening a wall for war is the oldest and most concrete branch of the strong image.
senses.whyCN: 为战争而加固城墙，是「变强」这一意象最古老也最具体的一支。

senses.title: Add strength to food
senses.definition: to add vitamins or minerals to food so that it gives more health benefit
senses.definitionCN: 在食物中添加维生素或矿物质，使其更有益健康
senses.example: Many cereals are fortified with iron and folic acid.
senses.exampleCN: 许多麦片都添加了铁和叶酸。
senses.why: Modern nutrition borrows the strong image, making the food itself stronger for the body.
senses.whyCN: 现代营养学借用了「变强」的意象，把食物本身做得对身体更有力。

senses.title: Strengthen the spirit
senses.definition: to give someone courage, confidence, or determination
senses.definitionCN: 给某人勇气、信心或决心
senses.example: The letters from home fortified her during the long training.
senses.exampleCN: 在漫长的训练期间，家书给了她力量。
senses.why: Once walls and bodies are strong, the same verb extends to the mind and the will.
senses.whyCN: 城墙与身体都能变强之后，同一个动词便延伸到心智与意志。

intro.en: Fortify comes from Latin fortis, strong, plus facere, to make, through Old French fortifier.
intro.cn: fortify 来自拉丁语 fortis（强）加 facere（做、使），经古法语 fortifier 进入英语。

items.en: Fortis means strong, the root behind fortitude and fortress.
items.cn: fortis 意为强，是 fortitude 与 fortress 的词根。

items.en: Facere means to make or to do, and it supplies the -fy ending.
items.cn: facere 意为做、使，提供 -fy 这一词尾。

items.en: Fortificare joins the two into the sense of making strong.
items.cn: fortificare 把两者合起来，意为「使坚固」。

items.en: Old French fortifier carries the verb into wider use.
items.cn: 古法语 fortifier 让这个动词被更广泛地使用。

items.en: Middle English fortifien is used first of walls and towns.
items.cn: 中古英语 fortifien 最先用于城墙与城镇。

items.en: Food fortification and figurative uses appear in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 食品强化与比喻用法在二十世纪出现。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the fort- family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of making something stronger.
note.cn: 形近组汇集 fort- 词族；近义组汇集表示「使更强」的动词。

entries.definition: Courage and strength in bearing pain or trouble.
entries.definitionCN: 在痛苦或困境中承受的坚毅；与 fortify 同出 fortis，并非同一词。

entries.definition: A strong building or town made for defence.
entries.definitionCN: 为防御而建的坚固堡垒或要塞；与 fortify 共享 fortis 词根。

entries.definition: The act of strengthening a place, or a defensive work built for it.
entries.definitionCN: 加固地点这一行为，或为此修筑的防御工事；由 fortify 加词尾构成。

entries.definition: To make something stronger or more solid.
entries.definitionCN: 加强；使更坚固，是最通用的说法。

entries.definition: To make something stronger, often by adding extra material or people.
entries.definitionCN: 加固；增援，常指追加材料或人手。

entries.definition: To support and improve something that is weak or failing.
entries.definitionCN: 支撑并提振衰弱或正在下滑的事物。

normalIntro.en: Fortify is fortis plus facere: to make strong, whether a wall, a food, or a mood.
normalIntro.cn: fortify 是 fortis 加 facere：把墙、食物或心绪都做得更强。

normal.en: Fortis is strong, and -fy means to make.
normal.cn: fortis 是强，-fy 是使……。

normal.en: A fortified wall is one that has been made stronger.
normal.cn: fortified wall 就是被加固过的墙。

normal.en: Fortified cereal has extra vitamins added to it.
normal.cn: fortified cereal 是添加了额外维生素的麦片。

normal.en: Fortitude is the noun for the strength itself.
normal.cn: fortitude 是表示「坚毅」本身的名词。

normal.en: Compare reinforce: reinforce adds material, while fortify makes the whole stronger.
normal.cn: 对比 reinforce：reinforce 是追加材料，fortify 是整体变强。

abstract.en: See masons filling a cracked wall with fresh stones.
abstract.cn: 想象石匠往裂开的墙里填进新石块。

abstract.en: Picture a ring of towers rising around a town.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈塔楼在小镇四周立起。

abstract.en: Think of a glass of milk carrying tiny extra minerals.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯牛奶里多带了一些矿物质。

examples.en: The council fortified the bridge before the storm.
examples.cn: 市政会在暴雨前加固了那座桥。

examples.en: This flour is fortified with calcium.
examples.cn: 这种面粉添加了钙。

examples.en: Good news fortified the team for the final match.
examples.cn: 好消息让球队在决赛前更有士气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「佛提法」——像用一套法子把城墙和身体都变结实；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁 fortis（强）+ facere（做、使）→ fortificare（使坚固）→ 古法语 fortifier → 英语 fortify，核心义「使变强」。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses are one operation, making strong, applied first to stone, then to armies, then to food, then to the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项其实是同一个动作「使变强」，先用在石头，再用于军队、食物，最后落到人心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mason filling the gaps of a wall until it stands firm.
core.cn: 核心意象：石匠把墙的缝隙填满，直到墙体稳固。

branches.en: Stone and concrete made harder.
branches.cn: 石头与混凝土被做得更硬。

branches.en: Towers and ditches added for war.
branches.cn: 为战争而加筑塔楼与壕沟。

branches.en: Vitamins added to daily food.
branches.cn: 日常食物里添进维生素。

branches.en: Courage raised before a hard task.
branches.cn: 在艰难任务前提振勇气。

branches.en: One verb strengthens a place, a meal, and a person.
branches.cn: 同一个动词加固地点、强化餐食，也坚固一个人。

intro.en: Fortify joins the Latin root fortis to the suffix -fy, and the family runs through fortitude, fortress, and fortification.
intro.cn: fortify 把拉丁词根 fortis 接上词尾 -fy，词族延伸出 fortitude、fortress 与 fortification。

latinIntro.en: Latin fortis is strong, facere makes, and together they form fortificare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fortis 意为强，facere 意为做，两者合成 fortificare。

items.example: Fortis is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: fortis 是整个词族的基础。
facere 提供 -fy 词尾。
fortificare 以 -ficare 结尾。
fortify 以 -fy 结尾。
fortification 表示这一行为。

items.example: Fortifier names the person or substance.
items.exampleCN: fortifier 指做这件事的人或强化剂。
fortitude 保留「强」的意思。

items.example: Fortress is a place made strong.
items.exampleCN: fortress 是被造得坚固的地方。
fortified 出现在食品标签上。

latinEntries.exampleCN: facere 见于许多 -fy 结尾的动词。

definition_zh: 每两周一次的；每两周一次地；双周刊
definition_en: happening, appearing, or paid once in every two weeks
core_image: 日历上隔一格画一个圈，两个圈之间总空着一格
scene: 编辑部把周刊改成两周一期，老读者起初有些不习惯。The magazine moved to a fortnightly schedule last spring.
sceneCN: 这里 fortnightly 是「每两周一次的」（第 1 个义项：按两周为周期发生）；句意：这份杂志去年春天改成了两周一期的出版节奏。

pos.zh: 每两周一次的；隔周发生的
每两周一次地
双周刊

forms.label: 形容词与副词原级（无屈折变化）

derivatives.zh: 两星期；十四天（fortnightly 的基础名词，去掉词尾 -ly 即得）
双周刊（fortnightly 作名词时的复数形式）
两周一次的；一周两次的（美式常用说法，与 fortnightly 构词平行）

senses.title: Once every two weeks
senses.definition: happening, appearing, or paid once in every period of two weeks
senses.definitionCN: 每两周发生、出现或支付一次的
senses.example: The team holds a fortnightly planning session.
senses.exampleCN: 团队每两周开一次计划会。
senses.why: Fortnight is fourteen nights, and -ly turns that period into a repeating schedule.
senses.whyCN: fortnight 是十四个夜晚，-ly 把这个周期变成「每隔一个周期」的重复安排。

senses.title: At two-week intervals
senses.definition: once in every two weeks, used to say how often something happens
senses.definitionCN: 每两周一次，用于说明某事发生的频率
senses.example: The newsletter is published fortnightly.
senses.exampleCN: 这份通讯每两周出版一次。
senses.why: The same ending -ly also forms adverbs, so the word can answer the question of how often.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词尾 -ly 也能构成副词，所以这个词可以回答「多久一次」。

senses.title: A two-week publication
senses.definition: a magazine or newspaper that comes out once every two weeks
senses.definitionCN: 每两周出版一期的杂志或报纸
senses.example: The story first ran in a Glasgow fortnightly.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇故事最初发表在一份格拉斯哥的双周刊上。
senses.why: British publishing gave the adjective a noun life of its own, naming the paper by its schedule.
senses.whyCN: 英国出版界让这个形容词独立成名词，用出版周期来给刊物命名。

intro.en: Fortnightly is the old English phrase fourteen nights, contracted to fortnight, plus the ending -ly.
intro.cn: fortnightly 由古英语短语「十四个夜晚」缩合成 fortnight，再加词尾 -ly。

items.en: Feowertyne niht means fourteen nights, the old way of counting two weeks.
items.cn: feowertyne niht 意为十四个夜晚，是古代计算两周的说法。

items.en: The phrase contracts into fortnight, one word for two weeks.
items.cn: 这个短语缩合成 fortnight，用一个词表示两周。

items.en: Fortnightly appears as an adjective and adverb of interval.
items.cn: fortnightly 作为表示间隔的形容词与副词出现。

items.en: British periodicals adopt fortnightly in their titles and schedules.
items.cn: 英国期刊把 fortnightly 用进刊名与出版日程。

items.en: British and Commonwealth usage keeps the word, while American English prefers every two weeks.
items.cn: 英国与英联邦地区保留这个词，美式英语则更常说「every two weeks」。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the -ly schedule words; the near-meaning group holds the two-week and interval words.
note.cn: 形近组是 -ly 结尾的频率词；近义组是表示两周与间隔的说法。

entries.definition: A period of two weeks, chiefly in British English.
entries.definitionCN: 两星期；十四天，主要用于英式英语，是 fortnightly 的基础名词。

entries.definition: Happening or appearing once every week.
entries.definitionCN: 每周发生或出现一次的，与 fortnightly 共享 -ly 词尾。

entries.definition: Happening or appearing once every month.
entries.definitionCN: 每月发生或出现一次的，同样是「周期加 -ly」的构词。

entries.definition: Every two weeks, or sometimes twice a week.
entries.definitionCN: 两周一次的，有时也指一周两次的；美式英语中与 fortnightly 最接近。

entries.definition: Happening at regular intervals.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定间隔周期性发生的。

entries.definition: Happening at even, repeated intervals.
entries.definitionCN: 按均匀而重复的间隔发生的。

normalIntro.en: Fortnightly is fourteen nights plus -ly: one period ends, then the same period begins again.
normalIntro.cn: fortnightly 是十四个夜晚加 -ly：一个周期结束，同一个周期再来一次。

normal.en: Fortnight is fourteen nights, a native way to say two weeks.
normal.cn: fortnight 就是十四个夜晚，是「两周」的本土说法。

normal.en: Add -ly and the period becomes a schedule.
normal.cn: 加上 -ly，周期就变成日程。

normal.en: A fortnightly column appears twenty-six times a year.
normal.cn: 双周专栏一年出现二十六次。

normal.en: British pay slips often say paid fortnightly.
normal.cn: 英国工资单常写「paid fortnightly」。

normal.en: Compare biweekly, which can also mean twice a week.
normal.cn: 对比 biweekly，它也可能指一周两次。

abstract.en: See a calendar with alternate squares circled.
abstract.cn: 想象日历上隔一格圈一个。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose hand jumps two weeks at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟的指针一次跳过两周。

abstract.en: Think of a newsstand where the same title appears every other week.
abstract.cn: 想象报刊亭里同一本刊物隔周出现。

examples.en: The committee meets fortnightly on Tuesdays.
examples.cn: 委员会每两周在周二开一次会。

examples.en: Her fortnightly column covers new research.
examples.cn: 她的双周专栏介绍新的研究。

examples.en: The rent is paid fortnightly by direct debit.
examples.cn: 房租通过直接扣款每两周支付一次。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆开像 four-night-ly——十四个夜晚凑成两周，隔周再来一次；这只是谐音拆词联想，便于记忆。

root: 古英语 feowertyne niht（十四夜）→ 中古英语 fortnight（两星期）+ -ly（每……一次）→ fortnightly，核心义「以十四夜为周期」。

sensesIntro.en: One period of fourteen nights gives all three senses: the schedule, the adverb of frequency, and the publication named after its schedule.
sensesIntro.cn: 「十四个夜晚」这一个周期生出三个义项：日程、频率副词，以及按周期命名的刊物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a calendar with every other square circled.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历上隔一格画一个圈。

branches.en: A planning meeting on alternate weeks.
branches.cn: 隔周开一次的计划会。

branches.en: Wages arriving every second Friday.
branches.cn: 每隔一个周五到账的工资。

branches.en: A paper that appears twenty-six times a year.
branches.cn: 一年出二十六期的刊物。

branches.en: The adjective and the adverb share one cadence.
branches.cn: 形容词与副词共享同一个节奏。

branches.en: A publication is named for the interval it keeps.
branches.cn: 刊物按它遵守的间隔来命名。

intro.en: Fortnightly is a native English counting phrase plus -ly, and the items below show the words behind it.
intro.cn: fortnightly 是英语本土计数短语加 -ly 构成，下面列出它背后的词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin word is involved here, since the source is the Old English phrase fourteen nights.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词不涉及拉丁语，来源是古英语短语「十四个夜晚」。

items.exampleCN: fortnight 是基础名词。

items.meaning: every, or in the manner of
items.exampleCN: -ly 词尾标示间隔。

items.example: Fourteen nights is the old count.
items.exampleCN: 十四个夜晚是古老的数法。

items.meaning: the dark part of the day
items.exampleCN: 古人计的是夜晚，不是白天。
weekly 是最接近的同型词。
monthly 重复同样的构词。
biweekly 在意思上与之重叠。

items.example: Period names the idea behind the word.
items.exampleCN: period 表示这个词背后的周期概念。
interval 描述两次之间的空隙。

definition_zh: 论坛；公开讨论的场所；讨论会；（古罗马）广场；网络讨论区；法庭；集市广场
definition_en: a place, meeting, or medium where people exchange ideas openly, or an online site for discussion
core_image: 城市中心的一片空地，人们带着各自的问题走到同一处开口说话
scene: 傍晚的社区公告栏前，几位居民围着刚贴出的通知争论不休。The new online forum lets residents raise problems without leaving home.
sceneCN: 这里 forum 是「网络论坛」（第 5 个义项：供人在网上发帖讨论的讨论区）；句意：新的网络论坛让居民不必出门就能反映问题。

pos.zh: 论坛；公开讨论的场所；讨论会；（古罗马）广场；网络讨论区；法庭

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 forensis（属于广场的）而来，义为「法庭的；法医的」
由本词加表示「人」的后缀 -ite 构成，义为「论坛常客」
由本词与 goer 复合而成，义为「常逛论坛的人」

senses.title: The open square of a Roman city
senses.titleCN: 古罗马城市的公共广场
senses.definition: the central open square of a Roman city, used for markets, courts, and public business
senses.definitionCN: 罗马城市中央的露天广场，用于集市、审判与公共事务
senses.example: Cicero addressed the crowd in the forum.
senses.exampleCN: 西塞罗在广场上向人群发表演说。
senses.why: The Latin noun named the open ground in front of the buildings, the shared space where civic life happened.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁语名词原指建筑前的一片空地，是公共生活发生的共享空间。

senses.title: A place for open public discussion
senses.definition: a place where people can meet to debate matters of public interest
senses.definitionCN: 人们可以聚集起来辩论公共事务的场所
senses.example: The town square became a forum for arguing about the new road.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上的广场成了争论新公路的场所。
senses.why: A square where citizens gathered turned into the image of any space set aside for public speech.
senses.whyCN: 市民聚集的广场，转而成为任何为公共言论留出的空间的意象。

senses.title: A meeting held to discuss a subject
senses.definition: an organized meeting or conference at which a subject is discussed, often with an audience
senses.definitionCN: 为讨论某一主题而组织的会议，通常有听众在场
senses.example: The university held a forum on climate policy.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学举办了一场关于气候政策的讨论会。
senses.why: The physical gathering place gave its name to the gathering itself, so a forum can be an event.
senses.whyCN: 实体的聚会场所把名字让给了聚会本身，所以 forum 也可以指一场活动。

senses.title: A medium that gives space to public voices
senses.titleCN: 发表意见的媒介；舆论平台
senses.definition: a newspaper, broadcast, or other medium that offers space for open expression of ideas
senses.definitionCN: 为公开表达观点提供版面的报纸、广播等媒介
senses.example: The radio station is a forum for listeners from every district.
senses.exampleCN: 这家电台是各区听众发表意见的平台。
senses.why: Once the square becomes abstract, any channel that carries many voices works like that square.
senses.whyCN: 一旦广场变成抽象概念，任何承载众多声音的渠道就都像那片广场。

senses.title: An online discussion site
senses.definition: a website or section of a website where users post messages and reply to one another on shared topics
senses.definitionCN: 用户就共同话题发帖并互相回复的网站或网站版块
senses.example: She found the answer to her question on a language forum.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一个语言论坛上找到了问题的答案。
senses.why: The internet rebuilt the old square as a page of threads, keeping the same purpose of open exchange.
senses.whyCN: 互联网把旧日的广场重建为一页页帖子，保留了公开交流的同一目的。

senses.title: A court or tribunal
senses.definition: a court of law or a judicial assembly, especially in historical or formal use
senses.definitionCN: 法庭或审判会议，多用于历史或正式语境
senses.example: The case was brought before the forum of the province.
senses.exampleCN: 此案被提交到该省的法庭审理。
senses.why: Roman courts sat in the forum, so the place name came to mean the court that sat there.
senses.whyCN: 罗马法庭就设在广场上，于是地名转而指在那里开庭的法庭。

senses.title: A market square
senses.definition: a marketplace or market square in a town, now chiefly historical
senses.definitionCN: 城镇中的集市或市场广场，今多用于历史语境
senses.example: Farmers brought their produce to the forum each morning.
senses.exampleCN: 农民每天早上把农产品带到集市广场。
senses.why: The Roman square was first of all a market, and this trading sense survives in older writing.
senses.whyCN: 罗马广场首先是集市，这层交易含义在较早的文本中留存下来。

senses.title: The arena of public judgment
senses.definition: a setting in which a person or an idea is judged by public opinion
senses.definitionCN: 人或观念受到公众意见评判的场合
senses.example: The minister was tried in the forum of public opinion.
senses.exampleCN: 那位部长在舆论的法庭上受到评判。
senses.why: The old square held courts and crowds at once, so any public judgment can be pictured as a forum.
senses.whyCN: 旧日广场同时容纳法庭与人群，因此任何公众评判都可以想象成一座 forum。

intro.en: Forum comes from Latin, where it named the open square of a city before it named any meeting.
intro.cn: forum 来自拉丁语，最初指城市中的露天广场，后来才指会议。

items.en: *dʰwer- is generally reconstructed as "door, gateway"; the deeper origin of the root is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *dʰwer- 表示「门、出入口」；这个更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Latin foris meant "out of doors, outside", and fores meant "a door".
items.cn: 拉丁语 foris 意为「在门外、外面」，fores 意为「门」。

items.en: Forum named the open ground before a building, then the market and civic square of a city.
items.cn: forum 指建筑前的空地，继而指城市的集市与公共广场。

items.en: Forensis, meaning "of the forum", described the speeches and courts held in the square.
items.cn: forensis 意为「属于广场的」，用来描述在广场上举行的演说与审判。

items.en: English borrows forum for a place of assembly and debate; the online sense arrives in the late twentieth century.
items.cn: 英语借入 forum 表示集会与辩论的场所；网络义到二十世纪后期才出现。

items.en: Modern English extends forum to websites and to any channel of public discussion.
items.cn: 现代英语把 forum 扩展到网站以及任何公开讨论的渠道。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin square; the near-meaning group gathers words for public discussion and for public space.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁语「广场」词根构成的词；近义组收表示公开讨论与公共空间的词。

entries.definition: relating to courts of law or to the scientific investigation of crime
entries.definitionCN: 与法庭或犯罪鉴证有关的

entries.definition: the scientific investigation of crime, or the art of formal public debate
entries.definitionCN: 犯罪鉴证；正式辩论术

entries.definition: the Latin plural of forum, still used in formal writing
entries.definitionCN: forum 的拉丁语复数，仍用于正式文本

entries.definition: a raised place or a channel from which people express their views
entries.definitionCN: 高台，或借以表达观点的渠道

entries.definition: a conference or meeting at which specialists discuss a subject
entries.definitionCN: 专家讨论某一主题的会议

entries.definition: a place or setting of public activity, debate, or contest
entries.definitionCN: 公共活动、辩论或角逐的场所

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin square and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「广场」来源，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Forum is the Latin word for the open square; every later sense is that square reused.
normal.cn: forum 是拉丁语里「露天广场」的词，后面每个义项都是那片广场的再利用。

normal.en: Forensic comes from forensis, of the forum, because courts met in the square.
normal.cn: forensic 来自 forensis（属于广场的），因为法庭就设在广场上。

normal.en: An open forum is a meeting where anyone may speak.
normal.cn: open forum 是任何人都可以发言的会议。

normal.en: In computing, a forum is a page of threads instead of a square of stone.
normal.cn: 在计算机领域，forum 是一页页帖子，而不是石板广场。

normal.en: Compare symposium: both are discussion events, but forum stresses open access.
normal.cn: 对比 symposium：两者都是讨论活动，但 forum 更强调公开参与。

abstract.en: Picture a stone square with columns on every side, where traders and lawyers share the same open ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一片四面立柱的石板广场，商贩与律师共用同一块空地。

abstract.en: Picture a low platform at the edge of that square, where any citizen may step up and speak.
abstract.cn: 想象广场边上一座矮台，任何市民都可以登上去发言。

abstract.en: Picture a circle of chairs in a hall, with a speaker in the middle and listeners taking notes.
abstract.cn: 想象大厅里一圈椅子，讲者在中央，听众在记笔记。

examples.en: The planners opened a forum for residents to comment on the new park.
examples.cn: 规划者开设了一个论坛，供居民评论新公园。

examples.en: Ancient Rome put its courts, markets and speeches in one forum.
examples.cn: 古罗马把法庭、集市与演说都放在同一座广场里。

examples.en: Moderators removed the rude posts from the forum.
examples.cn: 版主删除了论坛里的粗鲁帖子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛若姆」——佛像前的广场上众人围坐议事：论坛、讨论场所。

root: 拉丁语 forum「露天广场、集市」与 foris「门外、外面」同源，一般认为来自原始印欧语 *dʰwer-「门、出入口」；广场既是市场，也是法庭与演说之地，因此这个词从「地方」长成「讨论与评判的场合」。

sensesIntro.en: Forum begins as a Roman square, becomes any place or event of open discussion, and finally any medium, website or arena of public judgment.
sensesIntro.cn: forum 从罗马的广场出发，变成任何公开讨论的场所或活动，最后扩展到媒介、网站与公众评判的场合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open stone square at the centre of a town, where people bring questions and speak in public.
core.cn: 核心意象：城镇中央一片开放的石头广场，人们把问题带到这里当众开口。

branches.en: THE STONE: the Roman square is the literal core of the word.
branches.cn: 石地线：罗马广场是这个词最字面的核心。

branches.en: THE GATHERING: a place of speech turns into an event of speech.
branches.cn: 聚会线：发言的场所转为发言的活动。

branches.en: THE VOICE: any medium or arena in which public opinion is heard.
branches.cn: 声音线：任何让公众意见被听见的媒介或场合。

branches.en: THE SCREEN: the online board rebuilds the square as pages of threads.
branches.cn: 屏幕线：网络讨论区把广场重建为一页页帖子。

branches.en: THE BUSINESS: courts and markets were the first work done in the square.
branches.cn: 事务线：审判与交易是广场上最早进行的事务。

intro.en: Forum is a Latin noun whose family runs through foris, forensis and forensic; English also coins forumite and forum-goer.
intro.cn: forum 是拉丁语名词，词族经过 foris、forensis 与 forensic；英语又造出 forumite 与 forum-goer。

latinIntro.en: Latin foris, forum and forensis are all recorded, so only the Indo-European root behind them is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 foris、forum 与 forensis 均有文献记录，只有它们背后的印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.example: Foris names what is outside the door.
items.exampleCN: foris 指门外的区域。

items.example: The noun first named the ground before a building.

definition_en: to bring up a child who is not your own, or to help something grow and develop
core_image: 一双把幼小的生命托在掌心、慢慢往高处送的手
scene: 福利院的走廊里，一位年轻女子蹲下来替孩子系好松开的鞋带。She and her husband decided to foster two children from the local shelter.
sceneCN: 这里 foster 是「抚养别人的孩子」（第 2 个义项：把孩子接到家中抚养）；句意：她和丈夫决定抚养当地救助站的两个孩子。

pos.zh: 抚养；寄养；培养；促进；鼓励；心怀
寄养的；代养的（只用于名词前）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -age 构成，义为「寄养；养育」
