senses.title: To feed and nurse a baby
senses.definition: to feed and nurse a baby or a young animal, especially at the breast
senses.definitionCN: 喂养、哺育婴儿或幼兽，尤指哺乳
senses.example: The ewe refused to foster the orphan lamb.
senses.exampleCN: 那只母羊不肯哺育这只失去母亲的羔羊。
senses.why: Old English fostrian meant to supply food and nourishment, so the word begins as a feeding act.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 fostrian 意为供给食物与营养，所以这个词最初是一个喂养动作。

senses.title: To bring up a child who is not your own
senses.definition: to take a child who is not your own into a home and raise that child
senses.definitionCN: 把非亲生的孩子接到家中抚养
senses.example: They fostered a boy for three years before he returned to his family.
senses.exampleCN: 他们抚养了一个男孩三年，后来他回到了自己的家庭。
senses.why: The feeding sense widens into the whole work of rearing a child, done for someone else.
senses.whyCN: 喂养义扩展为抚养孩子的全部工作，而且是为别人做的。

senses.title: To be brought up in a foster family
senses.titleCN: 被寄养；在寄养家庭长大
senses.definition: to grow up in the care of adults who are not your biological parents
senses.definitionCN: 在并非亲生父母的成年人照顾下长大
senses.example: The sisters were fostered by their aunt after the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 火灾之后，这对姐妹由姑妈寄养。
senses.why: This is the same act seen from the side of the child: the rearing happens to the child, so the verb turns passive.
senses.whyCN: 同一件事从孩子一侧看：抚养发生在孩子身上，于是动词转为被动用法。

senses.title: To help something grow and develop
senses.definition: to help a skill, quality, activity, or organization grow stronger over time
senses.definitionCN: 帮助技能、品质、活动或组织随着时间发展壮大
senses.example: Small classes foster real discussion.
senses.exampleCN: 小班教学能培养真正的讨论。
senses.why: The feeding image moves from bodies to anything that can be made to grow.
senses.whyCN: 喂养的意象从身体转移到任何可以使之成长的事物。

senses.title: To encourage a feeling or attitude
senses.definition: to cause a feeling, belief, or attitude to develop in people
senses.definitionCN: 使某种感情、信念或态度在人们心中发展起来
senses.example: The coach worked to foster trust among the players.
senses.exampleCN: 教练努力在队员之间培养信任。
senses.why: A feeling is treated like a young plant: give it warmth and time, and it takes root.
senses.whyCN: 感情被当作幼苗：给它温暖与时间，它就会扎根。

senses.title: To promote cooperation between people or groups
senses.definition: to encourage friendly links, dialogue, or cooperation between people or groups
senses.definitionCN: 促进人与人、群体与群体之间的友好联系、对话或合作
senses.example: The exchange programme fosters links between the two cities.
senses.exampleCN: 这个交流项目促进了两座城市之间的联系。
senses.why: When the thing fed is a relationship, fostering means giving it the conditions to last.
senses.whyCN: 当被喂养的东西是一段关系时，foster 指给它维持下去的条件。

senses.title: Used before a noun: of temporary family care
senses.definition: used before a noun to describe care of a child by adults who are not the biological parents
senses.definitionCN: 用于名词前，描述由非亲生父母照顾孩子的方式
senses.example: He spent four years in foster care before he was adopted.
senses.exampleCN: 他被收养之前在寄养体系中生活了四年。
senses.why: The verb becomes a fixed attributive word in phrases such as foster home and foster care.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词在 foster home、foster care 等短语中固定为定语用法。

senses.title: To keep a hope or ambition in the mind
senses.definition: to keep a hope, dream, or ambition in the mind and treat it as worth preserving
senses.definitionCN: 把希望、梦想或抱负留在心里，并认为它值得保存
senses.example: She had long fostered the dream of studying abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 她一直心怀出国留学的梦想。
senses.why: The oldest sense, giving food, turns inward: what is kept alive is a hope.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的「供给食物」义转向内心：被养活的那样东西成了希望。

intro.en: Foster is an Old English word for feeding and rearing, and its family is Germanic rather than Latin.
intro.cn: foster 是古英语中表示「喂养、抚养」的词，其词族属日耳曼语而非拉丁语。

items.en: *pā- is generally reconstructed as "to feed, protect"; the exact shape of the root and its later spread are uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *pā- 表示「喂养、保护」；这个词根的确切形态与后续分布不确定。

items.en: Fostor meant food, nourishment, and the rearing of the young.
items.cn: fostor 意为食物、营养以及抚养幼小者。

items.en: The verb fostrian meant to supply food, to nourish, and to bring up a child.
items.cn: 动词 fostrian 意为供给食物、滋养并抚养孩子。

items.en: Middle English keeps foster for feeding and rearing, and the word begins to appear in family phrases.
items.cn: 中古英语保留 foster 的「喂养、抚养」义，这个词开始出现在家庭称谓的短语中。

items.en: Foster becomes a fixed attributive word in foster father, foster mother and foster child.
items.cn: 在 foster father、foster mother、foster child 等短语中，foster 固定为定语用法。

items.en: Modern English extends foster to skills, feelings, cooperation, and online discussion.
items.cn: 现代英语把 foster 扩展到技能、感情、合作与网络讨论。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same rearing root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of feeding, raising and caring.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「养育」词根构成的词；近义组收喂养、抚养与照料类的动词。

entries.definition: the practice or state of being brought up by adults who are not the biological parents
entries.definitionCN: 由非亲生父母养育的做法或状态

entries.definition: a person who fosters a child or an activity
entries.definitionCN: 抚养孩子或扶助某项活动的人

entries.definition: a child who is fostered; an older and rarer word
entries.definitionCN: 被寄养的孩子，属较旧、较少见的说法

entries.definition: to care for and encourage the growth of a child, a skill, or a feeling
entries.definitionCN: 照料并促使孩子、技能或感情成长

entries.definition: to give food or the conditions needed for growth
entries.definitionCN: 供给食物或成长所需的条件

entries.definition: to bring up a child, or to increase something
entries.definitionCN: 抚养孩子；提高、增加

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English feeding root and the phrases foster actually forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语「喂养」词根，以及 foster 实际构成的搭配。

normal.en: Fostor was Old English for food, and feeding is where the word starts.
normal.cn: fostor 是古英语的「食物」，喂养正是这个词的起点。

normal.en: The family also gives food and fodder, so the root is about feeding.
normal.cn: 这个词族还给出 food 与 fodder，可见词根与喂养有关。

normal.en: Foster care, foster home and foster parent are fixed phrases in modern use.
normal.cn: foster care、foster home 与 foster parent 是现代英语里的固定搭配。

normal.en: A teacher fosters discussion; a gardener fosters growth; the verb is the same.
normal.cn: 老师培养讨论，园丁助长生长，用的是同一个动词。

normal.en: Compare nurture: nurture stresses care and training, while foster stresses helping growth.
normal.cn: 对比 nurture：nurture 强调照料与训练，foster 强调帮助其成长。

abstract.en: Picture a warm hand holding a bottle to the mouth of a lamb.
abstract.cn: 想象一只温暖的手把奶瓶送到羔羊嘴边。

abstract.en: Picture the small shoes of a child placed beside a new front door.
abstract.cn: 想象一双小鞋摆在一扇新家门边。

abstract.en: Picture a suitcase standing in a hallway of a house that is not home yet.
abstract.cn: 想象一只行李箱立在尚未成为家的房子的门厅里。

examples.en: Good schools foster curiosity rather than fear of tests.
examples.cn: 好学校培养好奇心，而不是对考试的恐惧。

examples.en: The couple fostered three children over ten years.
examples.cn: 这对夫妇在十年间抚养了三个孩子。

examples.en: Warm words can foster cooperation between rival teams.
examples.cn: 温和的话语能促进对立队伍之间的合作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛斯特」——佛前施食，把孩子养大：抚养、培养。

root: 古英语 fostor「食物、养育」与 fostrian「喂养、抚养」同源，一般认为可追溯到原始印欧语 *pā-「喂养、保护」，与 food、fodder 同属一个「供给食物」的词族；这个词根更早的形态不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Foster moves from feeding a baby outward: rearing a child from another family, helping skills grow, encouraging feelings and ties, and finally carrying a hope inside.
sensesIntro.cn: foster 从喂养婴儿向外扩展：抚养别人家的孩子、帮助技能成长、鼓励感情与联系，最后是把希望留在心里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand holds a small life and feeds it until it can stand on its own.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手托着幼小的生命，喂它直到它能自己站住。

branches.en: THE MOUTH: feeding is the literal start of the word.
branches.cn: 口腹线：喂养是这个词最字面的起点。

branches.en: THE HOME: rearing a child, seen first from the adult and then from the child.
branches.cn: 家庭线：抚养孩子，先从大人一侧看，再从孩子一侧看。

branches.en: THE GROUP: the same help given to skills, activities and relationships.
branches.cn: 群体线：同样的帮助给到技能、活动与关系。

branches.en: THE HEART: a feeling is fed until it takes root.
branches.cn: 内心线：感情被喂养，直到它扎根。

branches.en: THE LABEL: fixed phrases mark the public use, and the inward hope marks the private edge.
branches.cn: 标签线：固定短语标出公共用法，内心的希望则标出私人一端。

intro.en: Foster is a Germanic word built on an Old English feeding noun, and English adds -age, -er and -ling to extend the family.
intro.cn: foster 是日耳曼语词，以古英语的「食物」名词为基座；英语再加 -age、-er 与 -ling 扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Foster has no direct Latin ancestor or Latin descendant in its own line; the family is Old English and Germanic, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: foster 自身的传承里没有直接的拉丁语来源，也没有拉丁语后代；词族属古英语与日耳曼语，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: The noun supplies the idea of food.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供「食物」这一概念。

items.example: The verb is the direct ancestor of foster.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 foster 的直接前身。

items.example: The modern verb keeps both the feeding and the rearing sense.
items.exampleCN: 现代动词同时保留喂养与抚养两层含义。

items.example: Food belongs to the same feeding family.
items.exampleCN: food 属于同一个「喂养」词族。

items.example: Fodder is the animal branch of the family.

items.example: The suffix names the person who does the rearing.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀指进行抚养的那个人。
它构成 fosterage。

items.example: The noun names the arrangement rather than the act.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指寄养这一安排，而不是单个动作。

items.meaning: a person or thing of a kind
items.exampleCN: 它构成 fosterling。

items.example: The suffix marks the child who is cared for.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标出被照顾的孩子。

core_image: 一层油污浮在水面，气味顺着风钻进鼻子
scene: 球场上观众忽然站起来，指着手臂上的淤青大喊。The referee sent the defender off for a foul on the striker.

pos.zh: 污浊的；肮脏的；难闻的；腐烂的；恶劣的；不公正的
犯规；犯规动作
弄脏；污染；对……犯规

senses.title: Covered with dirt or waste
senses.definition: covered with dirt, waste, or harmful substances; not clean
senses.definitionCN: 覆有污物、排泄物或有害物质；不洁净
senses.example: The canal turned foul after the factory opened.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂开工后，运河变得污浊不堪。
senses.why: The Old English adjective meant filthy and rotten, and physical dirt is its first job.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语形容词本义是「污秽、腐坏」，物理上的脏是它最早的功能。

senses.title: Rotten in smell or taste
senses.definition: having an unpleasant or rotting smell or taste
senses.definitionCN: 气味或味道令人不适、已经腐坏
senses.example: A foul odour came from the bins behind the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房后面的垃圾桶传来一股难闻的气味。
senses.why: Rot is dirt that has gone further: the same word covers what has spoiled.
senses.whyCN: 腐烂是脏的更进一步：同一个词也覆盖已经变质的东西。

senses.title: Unfair or dishonest
senses.definition: unfair, dishonest, or achieved by breaking the rules
senses.definitionCN: 不公平、不诚实，或通过违反规则达成
senses.example: The committee found no evidence of foul play in the election.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会没有发现选举中有不正当行为的证据。
senses.why: A foul act was once simply a filthy one; the sense shifted from dirt to moral stain.
senses.whyCN: 不正当的行为原本只是「脏」的行为；词义从污物转向道德上的污点。

senses.title: An act that breaks the rules of a game
senses.definition: an act in a sport that breaks the rules, especially one that harms or blocks an opponent
senses.definitionCN: 体育运动中违反规则的动作，尤指伤害或阻挡对手的动作
senses.example: The referee awarded a free kick for the foul.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判因这次犯规判了一个任意球。
senses.why: Sport borrowed the adjective: a foul deed in a game became a countable foul.
senses.whyCN: 体育借用了这个形容词：比赛中的「脏」动作成了可数的犯规。

senses.title: To make something dirty or polluted
senses.definition: to make water, air, or a place dirty or polluted
senses.definitionCN: 使水、空气或某处变脏、受污染
senses.example: Runoff from the fields fouls the river every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 每年春天，田地的径流都会污染这条河。
senses.why: The verb turns the state of dirt into the act that produces it.
senses.whyCN: 动词把「脏」的状态变成造成这种状态的动作。

senses.title: To commit a foul against an opponent
senses.definition: to break the rules of a sport against an opposing player
senses.definitionCN: 在体育运动中违反规则、侵犯对方球员
senses.example: The forward was fouled just outside the penalty area.
senses.exampleCN: 前锋在禁区外被犯规了。
senses.why: The noun foul becomes a verb of contact: to foul is to do the foul thing.
senses.whyCN: 名词「犯规」转为接触性动词：to foul 就是做出那个犯规动作。

senses.title: Stormy or contrary, of weather and wind
senses.definition: of weather, stormy and unpleasant; of wind, blowing against a ship or an aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 天气恶劣、风雨交加；风向不利于船只或飞机
senses.example: The fleet waited in port for the foul weather to pass.
senses.exampleCN: 船队在港口等待恶劣天气过去。
senses.why: Sailing needed a word for conditions that ruin a passage, and foul already meant harmful.
senses.whyCN: 航海需要描述毁掉航程的条件的词，而 foul 本就有「有害」的意思。

senses.title: Obscene or offensive in language
senses.definition: of words or language, obscene, full of swearing, or deeply offensive
senses.definitionCN: 言语粗俗、充满脏话或极具冒犯性
senses.example: The teacher warned the class against foul language in the corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 老师警告全班不要在走廊里说粗话。
senses.why: Speech that breaks decency is pictured as speech that is dirty, so foul keeps its oldest image.
senses.whyCN: 破坏体面的言语被想象成「脏」的言语，foul 因而保留了最古老的意象。

intro.en: Foul is an Old English adjective for dirt and rot, and its moral and sporting senses grew out of that first filth.
intro.cn: foul 是古英语中表示污物与腐烂的形容词，道德义与体育义都从那最初的「脏」生长出来。

items.en: *pu- is generally reconstructed as "to rot, decay"; the form of the root and its spread are not fully certain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *pu- 表示「腐烂、朽坏」；这个词根的形态与分布并不完全确定。

items.en: *fūlaz meant rotten and filthy, and it is the source of German faul and Dutch vuil.
items.cn: *fūlaz 意为腐烂、污秽，是德语 faul 与荷兰语 vuil 的来源。

items.en: Ful meant dirty, rotten, and morally bad; it could describe food, water, and people.
items.cn: fūl 意为肮脏、腐烂、道德败坏，可形容食物、水与人。

items.en: Middle English keeps the physical and the moral senses side by side.
items.cn: 中古英语让物理义与道德义并排保留下来。

items.en: Sporting and nautical uses appear: a foul in a game, and foul weather at sea.
items.cn: 体育与航海用法出现：比赛中的犯规，以及海上的恶劣天气。

items.en: Modern English adds foul language, foul play, and the fouls of team sports.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了 foul language、foul play 以及团队运动中的犯规。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same filth root; the near-meaning group gathers words for dirt, rot and unfairness.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「污秽」词根构成的词；近义组收表示脏、腐烂与不公的词。

entries.definition: the state of being dirty, rotten, or unfair
entries.definitionCN: 肮脏、腐烂或不公的状态

entries.definition: a confusion or a mistake that spoils a plan
entries.definitionCN: 搞乱计划的混乱或差错

entries.definition: the act of making something dirty, or the matter that blocks it
entries.definitionCN: 弄脏的行为，或造成堵塞的污物

entries.definition: covered with dirt; the everyday word for what foul states more strongly
entries.definitionCN: 覆有污物的；日常用词，foul 的语气更强

entries.definition: extremely dirty, often in a disgusting way
entries.definitionCN: 极脏的，常含令人作呕之意

entries.definition: not treating people equally or by the rules
entries.definitionCN: 待人不等或不合规则的

normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语「污秽」词根，以及 foul 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Foul is the oldest English word for filthy; the moral sense grew out of the physical one.
normal.cn: foul 是英语里最古老的「污秽」词，道德义是从物理义长出来的。

normal.en: Foul play is dishonest conduct, especially in sport or in a crime story.
normal.cn: foul play 指不正当行为，尤其用于体育或罪案叙述。

normal.en: Foul weather is stormy weather; sailors still use the phrase.
normal.cn: foul weather 是恶劣天气，水手至今仍用这个说法。

normal.en: A foul in football is an act that breaks the rules.
normal.cn: 足球里的 foul 是违反规则的动作。

normal.en: Compare dirty: dirty is everyday, while foul is stronger and often literary.
normal.cn: 对比 dirty：dirty 更日常，foul 语气更强，且常带书面色彩。

abstract.en: Picture black oil spreading over a pond, with dead leaves stuck in it.
abstract.cn: 想象黑色的油污在池塘上铺开，死叶黏在里面。

abstract.en: Picture opening a fridge and meeting a wave of sour air.
abstract.cn: 想象打开冰箱时迎面扑来一股酸腐的气味。

abstract.en: Picture a player pulling a rival shirt where the referee cannot see.
abstract.cn: 想象一名球员在裁判看不见的地方拉扯对手的球衣。

examples.en: The air near the refinery smelled foul.
examples.cn: 炼油厂附近的空气闻起来很臭。

examples.en: The player was fouled inside the box.
examples.cn: 那名球员在禁区内被犯规了。

examples.en: Police are investigating possible foul play in the death.
examples.cn: 警方正在调查这起死亡事件中可能的不正当行为。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「发呕」——闻到那股味道就想吐：污浊、难闻。

root: 古英语 fūl「肮脏的、腐烂的」来自原始日耳曼语 *fūlaz（德语 faul、荷兰语 vuil 同源），一般认为可追溯到原始印欧语 *pu-「腐烂」，与拉丁语 pūs「脓」、pūtēre「腐烂」同源；更早的形态不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Foul starts as physical filth, passes through rot and bad weather, and then spreads to unfairness, rule breaking and dirty speech.
sensesIntro.cn: foul 从物理上的污秽出发，经过腐烂与恶劣天气，再扩展到不公、犯规与粗俗言语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a layer of oil and waste floating on water, with a smell that turns the stomach.
core.cn: 核心意象：水面浮着一层油污与废物，气味让人反胃。

branches.en: THE DIRT: physical dirt, and the act of making something dirty.
branches.cn: 污物线：物理上的脏，以及把东西弄脏的动作。

branches.en: THE NOSE: rot is dirt that has gone further, and the smell gives it away.
branches.cn: 气味线：腐烂是脏的更进一步，气味把它暴露出来。

branches.en: THE MORAL: dirt becomes dishonesty, and dirty speech becomes obscenity.
branches.cn: 道德线：脏变成不诚实，脏话变成粗俗言语。

branches.en: THE GAME: sport borrows the word for rule breaking and for contact with an opponent.
branches.cn: 比赛线：体育借这个词表示违反规则与侵犯对手。

branches.en: THE SEA: weather and wind that ruin a passage keep the old sense of harmful.
branches.cn: 海上线：毁掉航程的天气与风，保留了「有害」的旧义。

intro.en: Foul is a Germanic adjective; English adds -ness, -ly and a compound with up, while German and Dutch keep close cousins.
intro.cn: foul 是日耳曼语形容词；英语加 -ness、-ly 并与 up 组成复合词，德语与荷兰语则保留近亲。

latinIntro.en: Latin pus, putere and putridus are generally traced to the same reconstructed rotting root, though the Latin words are cousins rather than sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pūs、pūtēre 与 pūtridus 一般认为追溯到同一个表示「腐烂」的重构词根，不过这些拉丁词是远亲，而非来源。

items.meaningCN: 肮脏的；腐烂的；道德败坏的
items.example: The Old English word is the direct ancestor.
items.exampleCN: 这个古英语词是直接前身。

items.example: The reconstructed form is the Germanic base.
items.exampleCN: 这个重构形式是日耳曼语的基座。

items.example: The modern adjective keeps the physical core.
items.exampleCN: 现代形容词保留物理上的核心义。
它构成 foulness。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into a quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成性质名词。
它构成 foully。

items.example: The adverb describes how something is done.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词描述做事的方式。

items.example: The compound joins foul with the particle up.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把 foul 与小品词 up 组合起来。

items.example: German keeps a close cousin of foul.
items.exampleCN: 德语保留了 foul 的一个近亲。

definition_zh: 家禽；禽肉；野禽；水禽
definition_en: a bird, especially a domesticated one kept for eggs or meat, or its flesh used as food
core_image: 农家院子里拍翅的家禽，脚边散着谷粒
scene: 清晨的院子里，一群家禽围着食盆拍翅争食。At dawn the fowl flap around the feed pan in the yard.
sceneCN: 这里 fowl 是「家禽」（第 1 个义项：为取蛋或取肉而饲养的鸟）；句意：清晨的院子里，一群家禽围着食盆拍翅争食。

pos.zh: 家禽；禽肉；野禽
猎捕野禽（罕用）

derivatives.zh: 由 fowl 加表人词尾 -er 构成，义为「捕野鸟的人」
由 fowl 加 -ing 构成，义为「猎捕野禽」
water 与 fowl 复合，义为「水禽」
wild 与 fowl 复合，义为「野禽」

senses.title: A domesticated bird
senses.definition: a bird kept on a farm for its eggs or meat
senses.definitionCN: 农场上为取蛋或取肉而饲养的鸟
senses.example: The farm raises fowl for eggs and meat.
senses.exampleCN: 农场饲养家禽，以获取蛋和肉。
senses.why: Old English fugol meant any bird; on farms the word settled on the birds kept in the yard.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 fugol 泛指任何鸟；在农场上，这个词逐渐固定指院子里饲养的鸟。

senses.title: The flesh of a bird as food
senses.definition: the meat of a bird, cooked and served as food
senses.definitionCN: 鸟的肉，烹调后作为食物
senses.example: Roast fowl with herbs is a winter dish.
senses.exampleCN: 香草烤禽肉是一道冬季菜。
senses.why: Once a bird is killed for the table, fowl names the food rather than the living animal.
senses.whyCN: 鸟一旦被宰杀上桌，fowl 就指食物，而不再指活着的动物。

senses.title: Wild birds that are hunted
senses.definition: wild birds, especially those shot or trapped for food
senses.definitionCN: 野生的鸟，尤指为取食而猎捕的鸟
senses.example: Hunters wait at dusk for wild fowl.
senses.exampleCN: 猎人在黄昏等待野禽出现。
senses.why: The word kept its old general meaning of bird, and hunting speech used it for game birds.
senses.whyCN: 这个词保留了「鸟」的古老泛义，狩猎用语便用它指可猎的鸟。

senses.title: A bird of lake and marsh
senses.definition: a water bird such as a duck, goose, or swan
senses.definitionCN: 鸭、鹅或天鹅一类的水鸟
senses.example: Ducks and geese are water fowl.
senses.exampleCN: 鸭和鹅都属于水禽。
senses.why: Water birds were the wild birds most often seen and taken, so the compound became a sense of its own.
senses.whyCN: 水鸟是最常见、最常被捕的野鸟，因此这个复合词独立成一个义项。

senses.title: A bird, in older general use
senses.definition: any bird, as the word was used in older English
senses.definitionCN: 任何鸟，此为古旧英语中的泛称用法
senses.example: Every fowl of the air was named in the old poem.
senses.exampleCN: 那首古诗给空中每一种鸟都命了名。
senses.why: The modern narrow senses grew out of a broad old meaning that still survives in poetry and compounds.
senses.whyCN: 现代的几个窄义都从古老的宽泛含义长出来，这个宽义仍活在诗歌与复合词里。

senses.title: The guinea fowl
senses.definition: a spotted African bird kept for its meat, called guinea fowl
senses.definitionCN: 一种带斑点的非洲鸟，为取肉而饲养，称作珍珠鸡
senses.example: Guinea fowl roam the orchard at night.
senses.exampleCN: 珍珠鸡在夜里游荡于果园。
senses.why: Farm birds from other regions joined the family through compounds, and guinea fowl became a fixed name.
senses.whyCN: 外来的农家鸟通过复合词加入这个词族，guinea fowl 成了固定名称。

senses.title: A fighting cock
senses.definition: a rooster bred and trained for fighting, known as game fowl
senses.definitionCN: 为斗鸡而培育训练的雄鸡，称作 game fowl
senses.example: Game fowl were once bred for the pit.
senses.exampleCN: 斗鸡曾为斗鸡场而专门培育。
senses.why: Birds bred for sport were named with the same word, and game marked their purpose.
senses.whyCN: 为竞技而培育的鸟也用这个词命名，game 标明它们的用途。

senses.title: To hunt wild birds
senses.definition: to hunt or catch wild birds, a rare verb use
senses.definitionCN: 猎取或捕捉野鸟，罕用的动词用法
senses.example: They fowl the marsh in autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在秋天到沼泽猎鸟。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb in hunting language, naming the act of taking the bird.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词在狩猎语言中转为动词，指捕鸟的动作。

senses.title: Neither fish nor fowl
senses.definition: something that fits no clear class, from the fixed phrase neither fish nor fowl
senses.definitionCN: 不属于任何明确类别的事物，出自固定说法「neither fish nor fowl」
senses.example: The design is neither fish nor fowl.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计不伦不类。
senses.why: The idiom sets fowl against fish, so the word now also marks a thing that belongs to no proper kind.
senses.whyCN: 这个习语把 fowl 与 fish 对举，于是这个词也能指不属于任何类的东西。

intro.en: Fowl goes back to Old English fugol, a general word for a bird, and to Proto-Germanic fuglaz.
intro.cn: fowl 可追到古英语 fugol（泛指鸟）与原始日耳曼语 fuglaz。

items.en: A reconstructed root for flying or flowing is often cited behind the bird name, but the link is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为有一个表示「飞、流」的构拟词根在该鸟名之后，但这一联系并不确定。

items.en: Fuglaz is the reconstructed word for a bird, which yields German Vogel and Dutch vogel.
items.cn: fuglaz 是构拟的「鸟」一词，由此产生德语 Vogel 与荷兰语 vogel。

items.en: Fugol names any bird, wild or tame.
items.cn: 古英语 fugol 泛指任何鸟，不分野生与家养。

items.en: The form fowl appears, and the meaning narrows toward farm birds.
items.cn: 中古英语出现 fowl 这一形式，词义向农家饲养的鸟收窄。

items.en: Fowl settles into poultry, wildfowl, and waterfowl, with the meat sense beside them.
items.cn: 现代英语把 fowl 分入家禽、野禽与水禽，旁边还有表示禽肉的义项。

items.en: Farming and shooting writing fixes compound names such as game fowl and wild fowl.
items.cn: 农事与狩猎写作固定了 game fowl 与 wild fowl 这类复合名称。

note.en: Fowl sounds like foul and fool, and it sits near the everyday bird, poultry, and game words.
note.cn: fowl 与 foul、fool 读音或拼写相近，意义上则靠近 bird、poultry、game 这些日常词。

entries.definition: dirty, unpleasant, or against the rules
entries.definitionCN: 肮脏的、令人不快的或犯规的；与 fowl 只是读音相同、拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a person who lacks good sense
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏判断力的人；与 fowl 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a person who hunts wild birds
entries.definitionCN: 捕猎野鸟的人

entries.definition: farm birds kept for their eggs or meat
entries.definitionCN: 为取蛋或取肉而饲养的农家鸟

entries.definition: a feathered animal with wings
entries.definitionCN: 有羽毛和翅膀的动物

entries.definition: wild animals hunted for food
entries.definitionCN: 为取食而猎捕的野生动物

normalIntro.en: Fowl is the farmyard word for birds, carried down from Old English fugol.
normalIntro.cn: fowl 是农家院子里指鸟的词，从古英语 fugol 一路传来。

normal.en: Old English fugol meant any bird, and German Vogel is its close cousin.
normal.cn: 古英语 fugol 泛指任何鸟，德语 Vogel 是它的近亲同族词。

normal.en: A farm that keeps fowl keeps chickens, ducks, or geese.
normal.cn: keep fowl 的农场养的是鸡、鸭或鹅。

normal.en: Wild fowl and water fowl name the birds of marsh and lake.
normal.cn: wild fowl 与 water fowl 指沼泽和湖面上的鸟。

normal.en: Guinea fowl and game fowl are fixed names for particular birds.
normal.cn: guinea fowl 与 game fowl 是特定鸟类的固定名称。

normal.en: Neither fish nor fowl describes something that fits no class.
normal.cn: neither fish nor fowl 形容不属于任何类别的东西。

abstract.en: Picture grain scattered in a farmyard and birds dropping down to feed.
abstract.cn: 想象谷粒撒在农家院子里，鸟群落下来啄食。

abstract.en: See a roasted bird carried to the table on a warm platter.
abstract.cn: 想象一只烤好的鸟被放在热腾腾的盘子里端上餐桌。

abstract.en: Hear shots at dusk over a marsh where wild birds rise.
abstract.cn: 想象黄昏的沼泽上枪声响起，野鸟四散惊飞。

examples.en: The farm keeps fowl for eggs and meat.
examples.cn: 农场饲养家禽，以获取蛋和肉。

examples.en: Wild fowl gather on the lake in winter.
examples.cn: 冬季野禽聚集在湖面上。

examples.en: The dish is made with guinea fowl.
examples.cn: 这道菜用珍珠鸡做成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fowl」听起来像「否」——问一句这是野鸟吗，答一句「否」，那是家禽；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 fugol（任何鸟）→ 中古英语 fowl → 现代英语 fowl，核心义从「鸟」收窄为「家禽、野禽」，与德语 Vogel 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Fowl starts as the general word for a bird, narrows to farm birds and their meat, and branches into hunted, water, and named birds.
sensesIntro.cn: fowl 最初泛指鸟，后收窄指农家鸟及其肉，再分出猎禽、水禽与各类专名鸟。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: poultry flapping around a feed pan in a farmyard.
core.cn: 核心意象：农家院子里围着食盆拍翅的家禽。

branches.en: The farm bird is the everyday sense of the word.
branches.cn: 农家鸟是这个词的日常义项。

branches.en: Once killed, the bird becomes meat on the table.
branches.cn: 鸟被宰杀之后便成为桌上的肉。

branches.en: Hunting and waterside life keep the wild and water senses alive.
branches.cn: 狩猎与水域生活让野禽与水禽义项延续下来。

branches.en: The old broad sense of any bird survives in poetry and compounds.
branches.cn: 泛指任何鸟的古老宽义仍活在诗歌与复合词中。

branches.en: Named birds, sport birds, the hunting verb, and the idiom all grow from the same word.
branches.cn: 专名鸟、斗鸡、狩猎动词与习语都从同一个词长出来。

intro.en: Fowl is a Germanic farm word, and English builds fowler, fowling, waterfowl, and wildfowl around it.
intro.cn: fowl 是日耳曼语系的农家词，英语围绕它构成 fowler、fowling、waterfowl 与 wildfowl。

latinIntro.en: Fowl has no Latin source at all; it comes from Old English fugol, so no Latin kin are listed here.
latinIntro.cn: fowl 完全没有拉丁语来源，它出自古英语 fugol，因此这里不列拉丁同源词。

items.meaning: a bird, especially a farm bird
items.example: Fowl is the headword of this family.
items.exampleCN: fowl 是这个词族的中心词。

items.example: Fugol is the Old English ancestor.
items.exampleCN: fugol 是古英语的祖先形式。
词尾 -er 构成 fowler。

items.example: A fowler takes wild birds in the marsh.
items.exampleCN: fowler 指在沼泽里捕野鸟的人。
词尾 -ing 构成 fowling。

items.example: Fowling is an old country pursuit.
items.exampleCN: fowling 是一项古老的乡间活动。

items.meaning: birds that swim on lakes and rivers
items.exampleCN: waterfowl 指聚集在湖上的水鸟。
wildfowl 需要安静的沼泽。

items.example: Game fowl were bred for the pit.
items.exampleCN: game fowl 指为斗鸡场培育的雄鸡。

definition_zh: 狐狸般的；狡猾的；妩媚的；红棕色的
definition_en: like a fox, especially in being cunning, attractive, or reddish brown
core_image: 一只红狐从树影里探出头，眼睛亮而机警
scene: 黄昏的林边，一只红狐从灌木后探出头，耳朵高高竖起。At dusk a foxy face with quick eyes rises above the bushes.
sceneCN: 这里 foxy 是「狐狸般的」（第 1 个义项：外貌像狐狸的）；句意：黄昏的林边，一张狐狸般的脸从灌木上方探出，眼睛十分机警。

pos.zh: 狐狸般的；狡猾的；妩媚的

derivatives.zh: foxy 加名词词尾 -ness 构成，义为「狐狸般的样子；狡猾」
foxy 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，义为「狐狸般地；狡猾地」
foxy 的基础名词，义为「狐狸」
fox 加 -ed 构成，义为「书页因年久发褐斑的」

senses.title: Like a fox in appearance
senses.definition: resembling a fox, especially in a pointed face or a reddish coat
senses.definitionCN: 外貌像狐狸，尤指尖脸或红棕色毛
senses.example: The dog has a foxy face and pointed ears.
senses.exampleCN: 这只狗有一张狐狸般的脸和尖耳朵。
senses.why: The suffix -y turns the animal name into a description: whatever looks like a fox becomes foxy.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -y 把动物名变成描述词：凡是像狐狸的，就成了 foxy。

senses.title: Cunning and crafty
senses.definition: clever at tricking others, in the manner of a fox
senses.definitionCN: 像狐狸那样善于欺骗他人
senses.example: A foxy dealer talked him into a bad contract.
senses.exampleCN: 一个狡猾的经销商说服他签了一份糟糕的合同。
senses.why: Foxes in fables win by tricks, so adding -y to the animal name adds a moral judgement.
senses.whyCN: 寓言里的狐狸靠诡计取胜，因此给动物名加上 -y，就带上了道德评判。

senses.title: Attractive in a bold way
senses.definition: sexually attractive, used informally of a woman
senses.definitionCN: 有性吸引力的，非正式地用于女性
senses.example: She wore a foxy red dress to the party.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿了一条妩媚的红裙去参加聚会。
senses.why: The fox also stands for a sharp, striking charm, and slang borrowed that image for looks.
senses.whyCN: 狐狸也象征一种锐利夺目的魅力，俚语便借这个形象形容外貌。

senses.title: Reddish brown
senses.definition: of a warm reddish brown colour, like a fox coat
senses.definitionCN: 像狐狸毛那样偏红的暖棕色
senses.example: Autumn leaves turn a foxy brown.
senses.exampleCN: 秋叶变成红棕色。
senses.why: The colour sense comes straight from the coat, the most visible fox feature.
senses.whyCN: 颜色义项直接来自毛色，那是狐狸最显眼的特征。

senses.title: Having the smell of a fox
senses.definition: having the sharp musky smell of a fox
senses.definitionCN: 带有狐狸那种刺鼻的麝香味
senses.example: The old blanket had a foxy smell.
senses.exampleCN: 那条旧毯子有一股狐骚味。
senses.why: Hunting and farm talk named the scent after the animal that left it.
senses.whyCN: 狩猎与农家的说法用留下气味的动物来给气味命名。

senses.title: Discoloured timber
senses.definition: of wood, stained reddish brown by fungus, in forestry use
senses.definitionCN: 林业用语，指木材被真菌染成红棕色
senses.example: Foxy boards were rejected by the sawmill.
senses.exampleCN: 变色的木板被锯木厂拒收。
senses.why: A trade borrowed the colour word for a defect that mimics a fox coat.
senses.whyCN: 某个行业借用了这个颜色词，指一种类似狐毛颜色的缺陷。

senses.title: A wine defect
senses.definition: of wine, having an odd fox-like smell from a chemical in the cork or the fruit
senses.definitionCN: 葡萄酒带有类似狐狸的怪味，源自软木或果实中的某种化学成分
senses.example: The tasters marked the bottle as foxy.
senses.exampleCN: 品酒师把这瓶酒标为带狐味。
senses.why: Wine judges needed a word for a smell near the animal scent, and reused foxy.
senses.whyCN: 品酒师需要形容一种近似狐骚的气味，便复用了 foxy。

senses.title: Shrewd and quick to see advantage
senses.definition: shrewd and quick to notice an advantage, often used with approval
senses.definitionCN: 精明而善于发现有利之处，常含赞许意味
senses.example: A foxy buyer spots a bargain at once.
senses.exampleCN: 精明的买家一眼就能看出便宜货。
senses.why: The same fox cleverness can be praised rather than blamed, so foxy splits into a positive sense.
senses.whyCN: 同样的狐狸式聪明可以被称赞而不被指责，于是 foxy 分出一个正面义项。

intro.en: Foxy is simply fox plus the suffix -y, and fox itself is a Germanic animal name.
intro.cn: foxy 就是 fox 加词尾 -y，而 fox 本身是日耳曼语系的动物名。

items.en: A reconstructed word for a tail is sometimes linked to the fox name, but the link is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为有一个表示「尾巴」的构拟词与狐狸之名相关，但这一联系并不确定。

items.en: Fuhsaz is the reconstructed fox name, which also gives German Fuchs.
items.cn: fuhsaz 是构拟的狐狸之名，德语 Fuchs 也由此而来。

items.en: Fox names the animal, and the female is fyxen.
items.cn: 古英语用 fox 指这种动物，雌狐称作 fyxen。

items.en: Fox is common, and foxy forms from fox plus -y.
items.cn: 中古英语 fox 已很常见，foxy 由 fox 加 -y 构成。

items.en: Foxy widens from a fox-like look to colour, smell, and slang praise.
items.cn: foxy 从「像狐狸的样子」扩展到颜色、气味和俚语中的称赞。

items.en: The wine and timber trades add technical senses for a defect.
items.cn: 葡萄酒与木材行业增添了表示缺陷的技术义项。

note.en: Foxy sits beside fox and its family, and near words for cunning, charm, and reddish colour.
note.cn: foxy 与 fox 及其词族相邻，也与表示狡猾、魅力和红棕色的词相近。

entries.definition: the wild animal with a pointed face and a bushy tail
entries.definitionCN: 脸尖、尾巴蓬松的野生狐狸

entries.definition: of book pages, stained brown with age
entries.definitionCN: 指书页因年久而发褐斑的

entries.definition: a female fox
entries.definitionCN: 雌狐

entries.definition: clever at tricking people to get what one wants
entries.definitionCN: 善于用诡计得到想要之物的

entries.definition: secretly clever and hard to catch
entries.definitionCN: 暗中机敏、难以捉摸的

entries.definition: somewhat red in colour
entries.definitionCN: 颜色偏红的

normalIntro.en: Foxy is fox plus -y: the animal lends its look, its tricks, and its coat colour to the adjective.
normalIntro.cn: foxy 就是 fox 加 -y：这种动物把自己的样子、诡计和毛色都借给了这个形容词。

normal.en: Fox plus -y gives foxy, just as hair plus -y gives hairy.
normal.cn: fox 加 -y 得到 foxy，正如 hair 加 -y 得到 hairy。

normal.en: A foxy face has a pointed chin and quick eyes.
normal.cn: foxy face 是下巴尖、眼神机敏的脸。

normal.en: Foxy brown names the warm red brown of a fox coat.
normal.cn: foxy brown 指狐狸毛那种偏红的暖棕色。

normal.en: Wine tasters and timber graders both use foxy for a defect.
normal.cn: 品酒师和木材评级师都用 foxy 指一种缺陷。

normal.en: Foxiness is the noun and foxily the adverb.
normal.cn: foxiness 是名词，foxily 是副词。

abstract.en: See a pointed red face sliding out of a hedge.
abstract.cn: 想象一张尖尖的红脸从树篱里探出来。

abstract.en: Watch a fox cross a yard without waking the dog.
abstract.cn: 想象一只狐狸悄悄穿过院子，没有惊动狗。

abstract.en: Picture a bright red coat turning heads at a party.
abstract.cn: 想象一件鲜红的外套在聚会上引人注目。

examples.en: Her foxy grin told me she had a plan.
examples.cn: 她那狐狸般的笑容告诉我，她已有打算。

examples.en: The leaves turned a foxy brown in October.
examples.cn: 十月里树叶变成红棕色。

examples.en: Critics called the wine foxy and set it aside.
examples.cn: 评论家说这酒带狐味，把它搁到了一边。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「foxy」谐音「福气」——像狐狸一样有魅力的人似乎很有福气；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 fox（狐狸）← 原始日耳曼语 fuhsaz → 中古英语 fox + 词尾 -y → 现代英语 foxy，核心义「像狐狸的」。

sensesIntro.en: Foxy begins as a plain likeness to the animal, then borrows the fox for cunning, charm, colour, smell, and finally trade defects.
sensesIntro.cn: foxy 先表示单纯地像狐狸，再借狐狸指狡猾、魅力、颜色、气味，最后指行业里的缺陷。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red fox head with bright eyes looking out of a hedge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只红狐从树篱后探出头，眼睛发亮。

branches.en: Looking like the animal is the first and plainest sense.
branches.cn: 像这种动物的样子，是最早也最朴素的义项。

branches.en: Fox cleverness can be blamed as cunning or praised as shrewdness.
branches.cn: 狐狸式的聪明可以是受指责的狡猾，也可以是受称赞的精明。

branches.en: The animal charm becomes a word for attractiveness.
branches.cn: 动物的魅力变成形容吸引力的词。

branches.en: Coat colour and animal scent are borrowed straight from the fox.
branches.cn: 毛色与体味都直接从狐狸身上借来。

branches.en: Trades reuse the colour and smell senses for faults in wood and wine.
branches.cn: 行业把颜色与气味义项用于木材和葡萄酒的缺陷。

intro.en: Foxy is fox plus -y, and English extends the family with foxiness, foxily, and foxed.
intro.cn: foxy 是 fox 加 -y，英语又用 foxiness、foxily 与 foxed 扩展这个词族。

latinIntro.en: Foxy has no Latin source; fox is a Germanic animal name, so no Latin kin are listed here.
latinIntro.cn: foxy 没有拉丁语来源，fox 是日耳曼语系的动物名，因此这里不列拉丁同源词。

items.meaning: the wild animal with a bushy tail
items.example: Fox is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: fox 是整族词的基础。

items.example: The suffix -y turns fox into foxy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 把 fox 变成 foxy。
foxy 描述像狐狸的样子。
词尾 -ness 构成 foxiness。

items.example: Foxiness can mean charm or cunning.
items.exampleCN: foxiness 可指魅力，也可指狡猾。
词尾 -ly 构成 foxily。

items.example: Foxily is the rare adverb form.
items.exampleCN: foxily 是罕用的副词形式。

items.meaning: stained brown with age, of paper
items.example: Foxed pages mark an old book.
items.exampleCN: 发褐斑的书页是旧书的标志。

items.example: Vixen comes from Old English fyxen.
items.exampleCN: vixen 来自古英语 fyxen。

definition_zh: 易碎的；脆弱的；虚弱的；不稳定的
definition_en: easily broken, damaged, or destroyed
core_image: 一只薄胎瓷杯，指尖稍一用力就会裂开
scene: 桌上放着一只薄胎瓷杯，杯壁薄得几乎透光。The fragile cup must be carried with both hands.
sceneCN: 这里 fragile 是「易碎的」（第 1 个义项：稍受力就会破碎的）；句意：这只易碎的杯子必须双手捧拿。

pos.zh: 易碎的；脆弱的；虚弱的；不稳定的

derivatives.zh: fragile 加名词词尾 -ity 构成，义为「脆弱；易碎性」
fragile 加 -ness 构成，义为「易碎；脆弱」（较少用）
fragile 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，义为「脆弱地」（罕用）

senses.title: Easily broken
senses.definition: of an object, breaking or cracking with little force
senses.definitionCN: 指物体稍受一点力就破碎或开裂
senses.example: Handle the fragile glass with care.
senses.exampleCN: 小心拿这只易碎的玻璃杯。
senses.why: Latin fragilis means easily broken, and the first English sense stays with glass and china.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 fragilis 意为易碎，英语最初的义项就停留在玻璃与瓷器上。

senses.title: Delicate in body or health
senses.definition: of a person, weak and easily harmed by illness or strain
senses.definitionCN: 指人身体虚弱，易受疾病或劳累伤害
senses.example: The fragile patient needed constant care.
senses.exampleCN: 这位虚弱的病人需要持续照料。
senses.why: A body can break like a cup, so the image of the thin vessel moved from objects to people.
senses.whyCN: 身体也会像杯子一样破碎，于是薄器皿这一意象从物体移到了人身上。

senses.title: Easily destroyed or harmed
senses.definition: of a thing such as trust, peace, or a plan, easily damaged or ended
senses.definitionCN: 指信任、和平或计划等容易被破坏或终结
senses.example: The ceasefire is still fragile after months of talks.
senses.exampleCN: 经过数月谈判，停火依然脆弱。
senses.why: Abstract things are pictured as thin shells that a single blow can shatter.
senses.whyCN: 抽象事物被想象成薄壳，一击即碎。

senses.title: Unstable and precarious
senses.definition: of a situation or market, likely to change or fail suddenly
senses.definitionCN: 指局势或市场可能突然变化或崩溃
senses.example: The fragile economy worries small shops.
senses.exampleCN: 脆弱的经济让小店铺担忧。
senses.why: Something fragile cannot bear pressure, so the word names systems that may collapse under strain.
senses.whyCN: 易碎之物承受不住压力，于是这个词也指在重压下可能崩溃的体系。

senses.title: Slender and finely made
senses.definition: of a structure or form, thin, light, and finely shaped
senses.definitionCN: 指结构或形体细薄轻巧、造型精细
senses.example: The insect has fragile wings.
senses.exampleCN: 这只昆虫有纤薄的翅膀。
senses.why: Thinness explains both beauty and breakability, so delicate shapes came to share the word.
senses.whyCN: 薄既解释了美，也解释了易碎，因此精细的形体也共用这个词。

senses.title: Faint in sound
senses.definition: of a voice or sound, weak and easily lost
senses.definitionCN: 指嗓音或声音微弱、容易消失
senses.example: Her fragile voice hardly reached the back row.
senses.exampleCN: 她微弱的声音几乎传不到后排。
senses.why: A sound that may vanish at any moment feels as breakable as thin glass.
senses.whyCN: 随时可能消失的声音，像薄玻璃一样易碎。

senses.title: Goods marked as breakable
senses.definition: goods packed and labelled as breakable, as in fragile cargo
senses.definitionCN: 指按易碎品包装并标注的货物，如「fragile cargo」
senses.example: Fragile goods travel in padded boxes.
senses.exampleCN: 易碎品装在加垫的箱子里运输。
senses.why: Shipping turned the adjective into a label, so the word now names a class of cargo.
senses.whyCN: 运输业把这个形容词变成标签，于是它现在指一类货物。

senses.title: Fragile X syndrome
senses.definition: a genetic condition called fragile X syndrome, named for the look of one chromosome
senses.definitionCN: 一种名为脆性 X 综合征的遗传病，得名于某条染色体的外观
senses.example: Fragile X syndrome affects speech and learning.
senses.exampleCN: 脆性 X 综合征影响语言与学习。
senses.why: Medical naming borrowed the word for a chromosome that looks brittle under the microscope.
senses.whyCN: 医学命名借用了这个词，指在显微镜下看起来易断裂的染色体。

intro.en: Fragile comes from Latin fragilis, easily broken, built on the verb frangere, to break.
intro.cn: fragile 来自拉丁语 fragilis（易碎的），由动词 frangere（打破）构成。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to break lies behind the Latin family.
items.cn: 一个构拟的「打破」词根位于这个拉丁词族之后。

items.en: Frangere means to break, and its stem frag- carries the idea of shattering.
items.cn: frangere 意为打破，其词干 frag- 承载「碎裂」之意。

items.en: Fragilis describes whatever breaks easily.
items.cn: fragilis 形容容易破碎之物。

items.en: French fragile carries the adjective toward English.
items.cn: 法语 fragile 把这个形容词带向英语。

items.en: Fragile spreads from glass and china to health, peace, and markets.
items.cn: fragile 从玻璃与瓷器扩展到身体、和平与市场。

items.en: Medicine names fragile X syndrome, and shipping prints fragile on parcels.
items.cn: 医学命名了脆性 X 综合征，运输业则把 fragile 印在包裹上。

note.en: Fragile shares its Latin root with fracture and fragment, and stands near words for delicacy and brittleness.
note.cn: fragile 与 fracture、fragment 共享拉丁词根，意义上靠近表示纤弱与易碎的说法。

entries.definition: the quality of being easily broken
entries.definitionCN: 易碎、脆弱的性质

entries.definition: weak and delicate, especially of a person
entries.definitionCN: 虚弱纤薄的，尤指人；与 fragile 同出拉丁语 fragilis，是法语渠道的双式词

entries.definition: a small piece broken off something
entries.definitionCN: 从某物上打下来的碎片

entries.definition: easily damaged and finely made
entries.definitionCN: 精细而容易损坏的

entries.definition: hard but snapping easily without bending
entries.definitionCN: 坚硬但一掰就断、不会弯曲的

entries.definition: able to be broken, often of goods
entries.definitionCN: 可以被打破的，常用于货物

normalIntro.en: Fragile is Latin fragilis, easily broken, and the root frag- runs through fracture and fragment.
normalIntro.cn: fragile 就是拉丁语 fragilis（易碎的），词根 frag- 贯穿 fracture 与 fragment。

normal.en: The root frag- means break, as in fracture and fragment.
normal.cn: 词根 frag- 意为打破，fracture 与 fragment 都含这个意思。

normal.en: Fragility is the noun, and fragilely is the rare adverb.
normal.cn: fragility 是名词，fragilely 是罕用的副词。

normal.en: Parcels marked fragile are stacked on top of the load.
normal.cn: 标着 fragile 的包裹会被放在货物最上层。

normal.en: A fragile peace or a fragile economy can fail under pressure.
normal.cn: fragile peace 或 fragile economy 都会在压力下崩溃。

normal.en: Frail is a French doublet of fragile, from the same Latin word.
normal.cn: frail 是 fragile 经法语而来的双式词，出自同一个拉丁词。

abstract.en: See a thin porcelain cup held between two fingers.
abstract.cn: 想象一只薄瓷杯被两根手指夹着。

abstract.en: Think of a dry leaf that crumbles at a touch.
abstract.cn: 想象一片干叶，一碰就碎。

abstract.en: Picture a fine thread holding two heavy stones together.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细线把两块重石连在一起。

examples.en: The fragile vase survived the move without a scratch.
examples.cn: 那只易碎的花瓶搬过来时一点也没磕着。

examples.en: Years of war left a fragile peace behind.
examples.cn: 多年战争留下一个脆弱的和平。

examples.en: Her health is fragile after the long illness.
examples.cn: 久病之后她的身体很虚弱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fragile」谐音「弗拉基尔」——联想一只薄瓷杯，稍一用力就裂；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 frangere（打破）→ 词干 frag- + 形容词词尾 -ilis → fragilis（易碎的）→ 法语 fragile → 英语 fragile，核心义「一碰就碎」。

sensesIntro.en: Fragile begins with objects that break easily, moves to weak bodies and delicate shapes, then to peace, markets, and voices.
sensesIntro.cn: fragile 从容易破碎的物体开始，转向虚弱的身体与纤薄的形体，再到和平、市场与声音。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin porcelain cup that a fingertip could crack.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只薄瓷杯，指尖一按就会裂。

branches.en: An object that breaks under little force is the first sense.
branches.cn: 稍受力就破碎的物体，是第一个义项。

branches.en: A weak body borrows the image of the thin vessel.
branches.cn: 虚弱的身体借用了薄器皿的意象。

branches.en: Trust and markets are pictured as shells that pressure can shatter.
branches.cn: 信任与市场被想象成受压即碎的薄壳。

branches.en: Thin wings and faint voices share the same lightness.
branches.cn: 纤薄的翅膀与微弱的声音共享同一种轻。

branches.en: Shipping labels and medical naming turn the adjective into fixed terms.
branches.cn: 运输标签与医学命名把这个形容词变成固定术语。

intro.en: Fragile is built on Latin frag-, from frangere, with -ilis and -ity forming the wider family.
intro.cn: fragile 建立在拉丁词干 frag-（出自 frangere）之上，-ilis 与 -ity 构成更大的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin frangere means to break, and fragilis means easily broken.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 frangere 意为打破，fragilis 意为易碎的。

items.example: Frangere is the verb behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: frangere 是整个词族背后的动词。

items.example: The stem frag- appears in fragile and fragment.
items.exampleCN: 词干 frag- 出现在 fragile 与 fragment 中。
词尾 -ilis 构成 fragilis。

items.example: Fragilis passes through French into English.
items.exampleCN: fragilis 经法语进入英语。
fragile 保留了拉丁语含义。
词尾 -ity 构成 fragility。

items.meaning: the quality of being easily broken
items.exampleCN: fragility 指这种性质本身。

items.example: Frail is a doublet of fragile.
items.exampleCN: frail 是 fragile 的双式词。
fragment 共享「打破」词干。

definition_zh: 香气；香味；芬芳；香水
definition_en: a pleasant, sweet smell, especially one that comes from flowers or from a bottled perfume
core_image: 一枝刚开的茉莉，香气在静止的空气里慢慢散开
scene: 清晨的花园里，篱笆边的茉莉刚刚开放。The fragrance of jasmine drifted across the wet lawn.
sceneCN: 这里 fragrance 是「香气」（第 1 个义项：花朵散发的好闻气味）；句意是茉莉的香气飘过湿润的草坪。

pos.zh: 名词：香气；香味；芬芳；香水

collocations.zh: 香调（香水的前调、中调、后调）

derivatives.zh: 由本词换用形容词后缀 -ant 构成，义为「芳香的；有香气的」
由形容词 fragrant 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「芳香地」
由形容词 fragrant 加名词后缀 -cy 构成，义为「芳香」，现代英语中罕用

senses.title: A sweet smell
senses.definition: a pleasant, sweet smell, especially one that comes from a flower
senses.definitionCN: 令人愉悦的甜香，尤指花朵散发的气味
senses.example: The fragrance of jasmine filled the whole garden.
senses.exampleCN: 茉莉的香气充满了整个花园。
senses.why: Latin fragrare meant to emit a sweet smell, so the noun names the smell itself before it names anything that carries it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 fragrare 意为「散发甜香」，所以这个词先指香气本身，而不是承载香气的物品。

senses.title: A bottle of perfume
senses.definition: a liquid product, usually alcohol based, that gives the body or a room a pleasant smell
senses.definitionCN: 一种通常以酒精为基底的液体产品，让身体或房间散发好闻的气味
senses.example: She chose a light floral fragrance for the evening.
senses.exampleCN: 她为晚宴挑了一款清淡的花香型香水。
senses.why: Once the smell was prized, people bottled it, and the same noun moved from the scent to the product that carries it.
senses.whyCN: 香气一旦受到珍视，人们就把它装进瓶子，同一个名词便从气味转到承载气味的产品。

senses.title: The aroma of food or drink
senses.definition: the pleasant smell of tea, spice, wine or freshly cooked food
senses.definitionCN: 茶、香料、酒或刚出锅的食物散发的好闻气味
senses.example: The tea has a delicate fragrance of bergamot.
senses.exampleCN: 这茶有一缕淡淡的佛手柑香。
senses.why: Sweet-smelling plants fed the kitchen, so fragrance came to describe the inviting smell of what is brewed and cooked.
senses.whyCN: 芳香的植物走进厨房，fragrance 于是也用来形容冲泡与烹煮之物诱人的气味。

senses.title: A lingering trace
senses.definition: a faint smell that stays in a place or on an object after its source has gone
senses.definitionCN: 来源离开后仍留在某处或某物上的淡淡气味
senses.example: The fragrance of pine lingered in the empty hallway.
senses.exampleCN: 松木的香气在空荡的走廊里久久不散。
senses.why: Smell outlasts the flower, so the word naturally names the trace left behind rather than the source.
senses.whyCN: 气味比花活得更久，所以这个词很自然地指留下的痕迹，而不是来源本身。

senses.title: A pleasant atmosphere
senses.definition: a pleasant quality that seems to float in a place, like a scent in the air
senses.definitionCN: 仿佛飘浮在某处空气中的怡人特质
senses.example: A fragrance of old paper and wax hung over the bookshop.
senses.exampleCN: 书店里弥漫着旧纸与蜂蜡的气息。
senses.why: A room can feel the way a garden smells, so the scent image is borrowed for the mood of a place.
senses.whyCN: 一个房间给人的感觉可以像花园闻起来那样，于是香气意象被借来形容场所的氛围。

senses.title: A hint of something
senses.definition: a slight suggestion or trace of a quality, a feeling or a memory
senses.definitionCN: 某种特质、情绪或记忆留下的细微暗示
senses.example: Her letters carry a fragrance of nostalgia.
senses.exampleCN: 她的信里有淡淡的一丝怀旧气息。
senses.why: The faintest smell is barely there yet unmistakable, which makes it a ready image for a hint that cannot be measured.
senses.whyCN: 最淡的气味几乎不存在却又不容错认，正好用来比喻无法测量的细微暗示。

senses.title: A good name
senses.definition: a good reputation that survives a person, in literary or archaic use
senses.definitionCN: 在文学或古旧用法中指一个人身后留下的好名声
senses.example: The old doctor left a fragrance of kindness behind him.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老医生身后留下仁善的美名。
senses.why: Scripture and old poetry speak of a good name as a sweet odour, joining reputation to the sense of smell.
senses.whyCN: 经文与古诗把好名声说成一种馨香，把声誉与嗅觉连在一起。

senses.title: An aromatic material
senses.definition: an aromatic substance or compound made for soap, candles or other goods
senses.definitionCN: 用于肥皂、蜡烛或其他商品的芳香物质或化合物
senses.example: The factory blends synthetic fragrances for soap and candles.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂为肥皂和蜡烛调配合成香精。
senses.why: Modern industry treats the smell as a measurable material, so the plural names the compounds rather than the experience.
senses.whyCN: 现代工业把气味当作可量化的材料，因此复数形式指的是化合物，而不是人的感受。

intro.en: Fragrance comes from Latin fragrare, to emit a sweet smell, through Late Latin fragrantia and Old French.
intro.cn: fragrance 源自拉丁语 fragrare（散发甜香），经晚期拉丁语 fragrantia 与古法语进入英语。

items.en: Fragrare means to emit a sweet smell.
items.cn: fragrare 意为散发甜香。

items.en: Fragrantia names the sweet smell itself.
items.cn: fragrantia 指甜香本身。

items.en: The French noun fragrance carries the word north.
items.cn: 法语名词 fragrance 把词带入北方。

items.en: English borrows fragrance, often through French, to name a sweet odour.
items.cn: 英语借入 fragrance，多经法语转手，用来指好闻的气味。

items.en: Poets and preachers use fragrance for reputation as well as for flowers.
items.cn: 诗人和布道者用 fragrance 既指花香，也指名望。

items.en: Perfumery and industry turn the noun into a product name.
items.cn: 香水业与工业把这个名词变成产品名称。

note.en: Fragrance is the Latin smell noun, with a small English adjective family and the everyday scent words beside it.
note.cn: fragrance 是拉丁语中表示气味的词，英语里有一个小的形容词词族，旁边还有日常的「气味」词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning sweet-smelling, built directly on the Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「芳香的」，直接由拉丁词根构成。

entries.definition: A rare noun for sweet smell, formed from fragrant with the suffix -cy.
entries.definitionCN: 罕用名词，义为「芳香」，由 fragrant 加后缀 -cy 构成。

entries.definition: Openly shocking or obviously wrong; it merely looks like fragrance and comes from another Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「公然的、骇人听闻的」；只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自表示「燃烧」的拉丁语动词。

entries.definition: A smell, especially a distinctive one left by an animal or a person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「气味、踪迹」，尤指动物或人留下的独特气味。

entries.definition: A liquid mixture with a strong pleasant smell, worn on the body.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「香水」，涂在身上、气味浓郁的液体调配物。

entries.definition: A strong pleasant smell, usually of food, coffee or wine.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「香气」，多指食物、咖啡或酒的浓郁香味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root and the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根，以及这个词实际保留的搭配。

normal.en: Fragrare is to smell sweet; the noun fragrance is that sweetness made into a thing.
normal.cn: fragrare 意为散发甜香；名词 fragrance 就是把这股甜香变成一件东西。

normal.en: The family is tight: fragrant, fragrantly and fragrancy all keep the same root.
normal.cn: 这个词族很紧密：fragrant、fragrantly、fragrancy 都保留同一词根。

normal.en: Perfume sellers talk about fragrance notes: top, heart and base.
normal.cn: 香水销售会讲香调，分前调、中调与后调。

normal.en: A fragrance-free product has no added scent at all.
normal.cn: fragrance-free 产品完全不添加香精。

normal.en: Compare aroma and scent: aroma is mostly food, scent is a trace, fragrance is often floral or bottled.
normal.cn: 对比 aroma 与 scent：aroma 多指食物香气，scent 多指痕迹，fragrance 常指花香或瓶装香水。

abstract.en: See a jasmine vine open at dusk and the still air turn sweet.
abstract.cn: 想象黄昏时茉莉藤开花，静止的空气变甜。

abstract.en: See a small glass bottle on a dressing table, its stopper still wet.
abstract.cn: 想象梳妆台上的一只小玻璃瓶，瓶塞还湿着。

abstract.en: See steam rise from a cup of bergamot tea and curl toward your face.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯佛手柑茶升起热气，弯弯地扑到脸上。

examples.en: The fragrance of roses drifted through the open window.
examples.cn: 玫瑰的香气从敞开的窗户飘进来。

examples.en: This candle has a warm fragrance of cedar and honey.
examples.cn: 这支蜡烛有雪松与蜂蜜的温暖香气。

examples.en: She sprayed a little fragrance on her wrist before leaving.
examples.cn: 出门前她在手腕上喷了一点香水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗瑞格伦斯」——花开满格，香气绕梁：香气、香水

root: 拉丁语 fragrare（散发甜香）→ 晚期拉丁语 fragrantia（香气）→ 古法语 fragrance → 英语 fragrance；同族词有 fragrant、fragrancy。另有一个形近词 flagrant 来自 flagrare（燃烧），只是拼写相近，词源不同。

sensesIntro.en: Fragrance starts as a flower smell, is bottled as perfume, moves into the kitchen, lingers as a trace, and then turns figurative for mood, hint, reputation and industrial material.
sensesIntro.cn: fragrance 从花香开始，被装进瓶子成为香水，进入厨房，留下余香，再转为比喻，指氛围、暗示、名声与工业原料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a jasmine flower opening, and the still air turning sweet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一朵茉莉开放，静止的空气变甜。

branches.en: THE FLOWER: the plain sweet smell is the first and most concrete sense.
branches.cn: 花朵线：单纯的甜香是最早也最具体的义项。

branches.en: THE BOTTLE: the prized smell becomes a product you can buy.
branches.cn: 瓶子线：被珍视的气味变成可以买到的产品。

branches.en: THE KITCHEN AND THE EMPTY ROOM: the smell of brewed things, and the trace that outlasts its source.
branches.cn: 厨房与空屋线：冲泡之物的香气，以及比来源更持久的余味。

branches.en: THE MOOD AND THE HINT: both borrow a faint scent for something that cannot be measured.
branches.cn: 氛围与暗示线：两者都借淡淡香气来指无法测量的东西。

branches.en: THE NAME AND THE FACTORY: reputation as a sweet odour, and smell treated as a material.
branches.cn: 名声与工厂线：把声誉说成馨香，也把气味当作材料。

intro.en: Fragrance is a Latin smell word with an English adjective family; suffixes do most of the building.
intro.cn: fragrance 是拉丁语中表示气味的词，英语里另有一个形容词词族，构词多由后缀完成。

latinIntro.en: Latin fragrare and fragrantia are recorded; the deeper Indo-European source is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fragrare 与 fragrantia 均有文献记录，更早的印欧语来源属于重构形式。

items.example: The verb is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的来源。

items.example: The noun names the smell itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指香气本身。

items.example: It forms fragrance from the Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 它让拉丁词干构成 fragrance。

items.example: English keeps the noun almost unchanged.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个名词几乎原样保留下来。

items.example: The adjective adds -ant to the stem.
items.exampleCN: 形容词在词干后加 -ant。
它构成 fragrantly。

items.example: The adverb describes how something smells.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词描写某物散发香气的方式。

items.example: The suffix -cy forms a rare noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -cy 构成一个罕用名词。
它构成 fragrance-free。
这个复合词形容未加香精的商品。

definition_zh: 虚弱的；脆弱的；易碎的；微弱的
definition_en: weak in body or easily broken, and so not able to last long or resist pressure
core_image: 一张被反复折叠的薄纸，轻轻一碰就从折痕处裂开
scene: 深秋的走廊里，护工扶着一位老人慢慢下楼梯。The frail patient stopped twice to catch his breath.
sceneCN: 这里 frail 是「身体虚弱的」（第 1 个义项：因年老或生病而体弱）；句意是那位虚弱的病人两次停下来喘气。

pos.zh: 形容词：虚弱的；脆弱的；易碎的；微弱的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ty 构成，义为「虚弱；脆弱；弱点」
由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「虚弱；脆弱」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「虚弱地；脆弱地」

senses.title: Weak in body
senses.definition: weak and delicate in body, especially because of old age or illness
senses.definitionCN: 身体虚弱单薄，尤因年老或患病
senses.example: The frail old woman needed an arm to reach the door.
senses.exampleCN: 那位虚弱的老妇人要人搀着才能走到门口。
senses.why: Latin frangere means to break and fragilis means easily broken; the body is pictured as something that could crack.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 frangere 意为「打碎」，fragilis 意为「易碎的」；身体被想象成一件随时可能裂开的东西。

senses.title: Easily broken
senses.definition: made of material that breaks or cracks under very little force
senses.definitionCN: 由受力很小就会断裂或开裂的材料制成
senses.example: The frail shell cracked as soon as it touched the rock.
senses.exampleCN: 那只薄脆的贝壳一碰到礁石就裂了。
senses.why: The oldest sense is literally about things that break, and the body sense grew out of that image.
senses.whyCN: 最早的字面义就是「会碎的东西」，身体义正是从这个意象长出来的。

senses.title: Morally weak
senses.titleCN: 意志薄弱的；易受诱惑的
senses.definition: easily led into wrongdoing because the will gives way
senses.definitionCN: 因意志退让而容易被引向错误
senses.example: He was not wicked, only frail, and he signed the false paper.
senses.exampleCN: 他并不坏，只是意志薄弱，于是签了那份假文件。
senses.why: If a body can break under pressure, a will can also give way, so frail moves from flesh to character.
senses.whyCN: 身体会在压力下断裂，意志也会退让，于是 frail 从肉体转到品性。

senses.title: Weak and unconvincing
senses.definition: too weak to persuade, especially of an argument or an excuse
senses.definitionCN: 尤指论点或借口太弱，无法说服人
senses.example: The case rested on frail evidence that the jury rejected.
senses.exampleCN: 这桩案子靠的是站不住脚的证据，陪审团没有接受。
senses.why: An argument is imagined as a structure that must carry weight; if it is frail, it collapses.
senses.whyCN: 论点被想象成承重的结构；一旦脆弱，就会倒塌。

senses.title: Slight in build
senses.definition: small and thin in body, with little strength to look at
senses.definitionCN: 身材瘦小单薄，看上去没有多少力气
senses.example: She looked frail beside the tall rowers, yet she pulled her weight.
senses.exampleCN: 她站在那些高大的桨手旁边显得瘦弱，却仍出了自己那份力。
senses.why: This sense keeps the body image but shifts from illness to mere size and thinness.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项保留身体意象，只是从病弱转到单纯的瘦小单薄。

senses.title: Brief and fragile
senses.definition: lasting only a short time and easily destroyed, as of peace or hope
senses.definitionCN: 只持续很短时间又容易被摧毁，如和平或希望
senses.example: Their frail peace held for one winter and then broke.
senses.exampleCN: 他们脆弱的和平只维持了一个冬天就破裂了。
senses.why: Something that can be broken soon is also something that cannot last long, so the word covers duration as well.
senses.whyCN: 容易破碎的东西也长不了，于是这个词也覆盖了时间上的短暂。

senses.title: Easily disrupted
senses.definition: of a system or arrangement, unable to withstand shock or change
senses.definitionCN: 指系统或安排经受不住冲击或变化
senses.example: The frail supply chain failed after a single storm.
senses.exampleCN: 脆弱的供应链在一场风暴之后就断了。
senses.why: Modern usage applies the breaking image to systems and structures rather than to bodies.
senses.whyCN: 现代用法把「会断」的意象用到系统与结构上，而不是身体上。

senses.title: Thin and trembling
senses.definition: of a voice or sound, thin and unsteady with age or emotion
senses.definitionCN: 指声音因年老或激动而细弱不稳
senses.example: His frail voice barely reached the back of the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 他微弱的声音几乎传不到大厅后排。
senses.why: A voice that trembles sounds like something about to break, so the same image covers sound.
senses.whyCN: 发抖的声音听起来像快要断的东西，同一个意象于是也覆盖声音。

intro.en: Frail comes from Old French fraile, from Latin fragilis, easily broken, from frangere, to break.
intro.cn: frail 来自古法语 fraile，源头是拉丁语 fragilis（易碎的），出自 frangere（打碎）。

items.en: Frangere means to break something into pieces.
items.cn: frangere 意为把东西打碎。

items.en: Fragilis means easily broken.
items.cn: fragilis 意为容易破碎的。

items.en: Fraile carries the sense of weak and delicate.
items.cn: fraile 带有虚弱、娇弱的意思。

items.en: English takes frail for bodies and for breakable things.
items.cn: 英语借入 frail，既指身体也指易碎之物。

items.en: Writers extend frail to arguments and to character.
items.cn: 十六世纪的作者把 frail 扩展到论点与品性。

items.en: Modern use adds frail systems, frail peace and frail voices.
items.cn: 现代用法又添上脆弱的系统、和平与声音。

note.en: Frail sits in the Latin break family, next to fragile and frailty, and close to the ordinary weakness words.
note.cn: frail 属于拉丁语「打碎」词族，与 fragile、frailty 相邻，也靠近普通的「虚弱」词。

entries.definition: Easily broken, usually of objects; the Latin adjective fragilis is its direct source.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「易碎的」，多指物品；直接来自拉丁语 fragilis。

entries.definition: The noun for weakness of body or of character.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「虚弱、脆弱」，指身体或品性上的弱点。

entries.definition: A piece broken off something larger; it shares the Latin verb for breaking.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「碎片」，与 frail 共享表示「打碎」的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: Not strong; the broad everyday word, with no image of breaking.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「虚弱的」，是最宽泛的日常词，不含「破碎」意象。

entries.definition: Fine and easily damaged, often with a sense of grace rather than illness.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「娇嫩的」，易受损，常带精致意味而非病弱。

entries.definition: Very weak, often of effort, sound or an old person; slightly more negative.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「衰弱的」，多指力气、声音或老人，贬义稍强。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root and the English break family that grew from it.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根，以及由它长出的英语「打碎」词族。

normal.en: Frangere is to break; frail is the state of being easy to break.
normal.cn: frangere 是打碎；frail 就是容易被弄断的状态。

normal.en: The break family: fragile, fragment and fracture all carry the same root.
normal.cn: 打碎词族：fragile、fragment、fracture 都带同一词根。

normal.en: Frailty is the noun, and it names weakness of body or of will.
normal.cn: frailty 是名词，指身体或意志上的虚弱。

normal.en: Frail health is a common pairing in medical writing.
normal.cn: frail health 是医学写作里的常见搭配。

normal.en: Compare weak and feeble: frail usually adds age, illness or fragility.
normal.cn: 对比 weak 与 feeble：frail 往往多一层年老、病弱或易碎的意味。

abstract.en: See a dry leaf on a windowsill, bending at a touch.
abstract.cn: 想象窗台上一片干叶，一碰就弯。

abstract.en: See a thin clay cup that cracks when hot water is poured in.
abstract.cn: 想象一只薄陶杯，倒进热水就裂开。

abstract.en: See a hand reaching for a pen and then stopping halfway.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸向笔，却在半途停住。

examples.en: Her frail grandmother needed help with every step.
examples.cn: 她虚弱的祖母每走一步都要人扶。

examples.en: The frail wooden bridge swayed under the truck.
examples.cn: 那座不结实的木桥在卡车下摇晃。

examples.en: Years of illness had left him frail and quiet.
examples.cn: 多年病痛让他变得虚弱而沉默。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗瑞尔」——纸薄一折就断：虚弱、易碎

root: 拉丁语 frangere（打碎）→ fragilis（易碎的）→ 古法语 fraile → 英语 frail，核心义「一碰就碎」；同族词有 fragile、fragment、fracture、frailty。

sensesIntro.en: Frail runs from a body that breaks under age, to objects that crack, to a will, an argument, a build, a peace, a system and finally a voice; each is something that cannot hold.
sensesIntro.cn: frail 从被年岁压垮的身体，到会裂的物品，再到意志、论点、身形、和平、系统，最后到声音；每一义都是「撑不住」的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin sheet of paper folded again and again until it splits.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张薄纸被反复折叠，直到裂开。

branches.en: THE BODY: a person who can no longer carry their own weight.
branches.cn: 身体线：一个再也撑不住自己重量的人。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the literal sense of a thing that cracks.
branches.cn: 物品线：会裂开的东西，这是字面义。

branches.en: THE WILL AND THE ARGUMENT: both collapse when pressure is put on them.
branches.cn: 意志与论点线：两者一受压就垮。

branches.en: THE FRAME AND THE VOICE: thinness seen in a body and heard in a sound.
branches.cn: 身形与声音线：单薄既看得见，也听得见。

branches.en: THE SHORT PEACE AND THE FRAGILE SYSTEM: things that cannot last or cannot resist shock.
branches.cn: 短暂和平与脆弱系统线：撑不久或扛不住冲击的东西。

intro.en: Frail is one word from a Latin breaking root, and English rebuilt a whole family of break words around that root.
intro.cn: frail 是拉丁语「打碎」词根传下的一个词，英语又围绕这个词根重建了一整族表示破碎的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin frangere, fragilis and fractus are recorded; the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 frangere、fragilis 与 fractus 均有文献记录，更早的印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.example: The verb is the breaking root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族的「打碎」词根。

items.example: The adjective gives Old French its form.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词给出古法语的词形。

items.example: The participle feeds fracture and fraction.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词衍生出 fracture 与 fraction。

items.example: Old French passes the word to English.
items.exampleCN: 古法语把这个词传给英语。

definition_zh: 兄弟的；兄弟般的；异卵双生的；兄弟会的
definition_en: relating to a brother, or warm and helpful in the way that a brother is
core_image: 两个年纪相仿的兄弟并肩站着，手臂搭在对方肩上
scene: 毕业典礼的草坪上，两个堂兄弟抱在一起很久。The fraternal embrace lasted until the photographer called time.
sceneCN: 这里 fraternal 是「兄弟般的」（第 1 个义项：属于兄弟或像兄弟一样的）；句意是那个兄弟般的拥抱一直持续到摄影师喊停。

pos.zh: 形容词：兄弟的；兄弟般的；异卵双生的；兄弟会的

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「兄弟会；兄弟情谊」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「兄弟般地」
由拉丁词干加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「亲善交往；称兄道弟」
由动词 fraternize 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「亲善往来」

senses.title: Of a brother
senses.definition: belonging to or coming from a brother
senses.definitionCN: 属于兄弟的，或来自兄弟的
senses.example: He kept his fraternal duty and paid the school fees.
senses.exampleCN: 他尽了兄弟的责任，付了学费。
senses.why: Latin frater is brother, and the adjective fraternalis was built to name whatever belongs to him.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 frater 是「兄弟」，形容词 fraternalis 就是为指「属于兄弟的东西」而造的。

senses.title: Brotherly in feeling
senses.definition: showing the warm affection that brothers are expected to have
senses.definitionCN: 表现出人们期待兄弟之间拥有的温暖情谊
senses.example: The old neighbour gave us a fraternal welcome.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老邻居给了我们兄弟般的欢迎。
senses.why: The adjective does not stay inside the family: any warm, protective kindness can be called fraternal.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词没有停在家里：任何温暖、护佑的善意都可以叫 fraternal。

senses.title: Of twins from two eggs
senses.definition: of twins that grew from two separate eggs and are no closer than ordinary siblings
senses.definitionCN: 指由两个独立卵子发育、亲缘程度与普通兄妹相同的双胞胎
senses.example: The fraternal twins look different and have different tempers.
senses.exampleCN: 这对异卵双胞胎长相不同，脾气也不同。
senses.why: Two brothers in one womb are the plainest image of brotherhood, so medicine uses the brother word for this twin type.
senses.whyCN: 同一个子宫里的两个兄弟是「兄弟关系」最直白的形象，医学便用这个词指这类双胞胎。

senses.title: Of a brotherhood society
senses.definition: of a society or order whose members treat one another as brothers
senses.definitionCN: 指成员彼此以兄弟相待的社团或组织
senses.example: The fraternal order has met in this hall for a century.
senses.exampleCN: 这个兄弟会组织在这座大厅里聚会已有百年。
senses.why: Clubs copied the family: members swore loyalty and called each other brothers, and the adjective followed.
senses.whyCN: 社团模仿家庭：成员宣誓效忠、互称兄弟，形容词也随之而来。

senses.title: Between nations or groups
senses.titleCN: 国家或团体之间兄弟般的
senses.definition: used of friendly relations between countries or organizations that treat each other as equals
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容国家或组织之间以平等相待的友好关系
senses.example: The two states signed a fraternal treaty on trade.
senses.exampleCN: 两国签署了一份兄弟般的贸易条约。
senses.why: Political rhetoric borrows the family image to make allies feel bound by more than a contract.
senses.whyCN: 政治修辞借用家庭意象，让盟友感觉彼此不只靠一纸条约相连。

senses.title: Of a religious brotherhood
senses.definition: of a religious community whose members live together as brothers
senses.definitionCN: 指成员以兄弟方式共同生活的宗教团体
senses.example: The fraternal community runs a school and a small hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 这个修士团体办了一所学校和一间小医院。
senses.why: Monastic houses were families of brothers before the word reached clubs, so this sense stays close to the root.
senses.whyCN: 修道院在词进入社团之前就是由兄弟组成的家庭，所以这个义项最贴近词根。

senses.title: Comradely among equals
senses.definition: warm and equal in tone, as among colleagues who act like brothers
senses.definitionCN: 语气温暖平等，像同事之间以兄弟相待
senses.example: There was a fraternal tone in the workshop, with no titles used.
senses.exampleCN: 车间里有一种兄弟般的语气，彼此不称头衔。
senses.why: The family image is stretched once more, now to any group of equals who share daily work.
senses.whyCN: 家庭意象再一次被拉伸，现在用于任何共享日常劳作的平等群体。

senses.title: Of a linked party
senses.definition: of a political party linked to another by shared aims and history
senses.definitionCN: 指因共同目标与历史而彼此相连的政党
senses.example: The two fraternal parties met to renew their old alliance.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个兄弟党会面，重修旧日的联盟。
senses.why: Parties use the brother word for allies abroad, keeping the family metaphor inside politics.
senses.whyCN: 政党用「兄弟」一词称呼海外盟友，把家庭隐喻留在政治内部。

intro.en: Fraternal comes from Latin frater, brother, through fraternus and the medieval adjective fraternalis.
intro.cn: fraternal 源自拉丁语 frater（兄弟），经 fraternus 与中世纪的 fraternalis 进入英语。

items.en: The reconstructed form bhrater underlies brother in English and frater in Latin.
items.cn: 重构形式 bhrater 是英语 brother 与拉丁语 frater 的共同来源。

items.en: Frater is the ordinary Latin word for a brother.
items.cn: frater 是拉丁语中表示兄弟的普通词。

items.en: Fraternus means brotherly, and fraternalis is formed from it.
items.cn: fraternus 意为兄弟般的，fraternalis 由它构成。

items.en: English borrows fraternal from Latin rather than taking it through French.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪前后直接从拉丁语借入 fraternal，而不是经法语转手。

items.en: Fraternal orders and fraternal societies appear in the records.
items.cn: 十七世纪的文献里出现兄弟会与兄弟社团。

items.en: Twins, nations and parties all take the adjective later.
items.cn: 双胞胎、国家与政党等用法都是后来才加上去的。

note.en: Fraternal belongs to the Latin brother family and sits beside the native word brotherly and the comrade word comradely.
note.cn: fraternal 属于拉丁语「兄弟」词族，与英语本族词 brotherly 以及表示同伴的 comradely 相邻。

entries.definition: A society of brothers, or the feeling of brotherhood; the noun from the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「兄弟会、兄弟情谊」，由同一词干构成。

entries.definition: To mix socially with others as if they were brothers, often used of soldiers and their enemies.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「亲善交往」，常指士兵与敌方称兄道弟。

entries.definition: The act of fraternizing, especially with an enemy or a group one should keep apart from.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「亲善往来」，尤指与敌方或本应保持距离的群体往来。

entries.definition: Showing the kindness of a brother; the native English word beside the Latin borrowing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「兄弟般的」，是本族语词，与这个拉丁借词并列。

entries.definition: Showing the kindness of a sister; the matching word for the other sex.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「姐妹般的」，是与之对应的女性版本。

entries.definition: Warm and equal, as among comrades; it stresses shared work rather than family.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「同志般的」，强调共同事业而非家庭关系。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root for brother and the family of words built on it.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「兄弟」词根，以及由它构成的词族。

normal.en: Frater is Latin for brother; fraternal is simply what belongs to him.
normal.cn: frater 是拉丁语的「兄弟」；fraternal 就是属于兄弟的。

normal.en: The family: fraternity, fraternize and fraternization all keep the brother stem.
normal.cn: 词族：fraternity、fraternize、fraternization 都保留「兄弟」词干。

normal.en: Fraternal twins come from two eggs, while identical twins come from one.
normal.cn: fraternal twins 由两个卵子而来，identical twins 由一个卵子而来。

normal.en: A fraternal order is a club that calls its members brothers.
normal.cn: fraternal order 是把成员称作兄弟的社团。

normal.en: Compare brotherly: brotherly is the home word, fraternal is the formal Latin one.
normal.cn: 对比 brotherly：brotherly 是本族语词，fraternal 是正式的拉丁借词。

abstract.en: See two brothers of the same height walking side by side, arms linked.
abstract.cn: 想象两个一样高的兄弟并肩走，手臂挽在一起。

abstract.en: See a hand steadying a younger hand on a stair rail.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在楼梯扶手上稳住另一只更年轻的手。

abstract.en: See two cradles side by side, each with its own blanket.
abstract.cn: 想象两张并排的摇篮，各盖各的毯子。

examples.en: His fraternal affection showed in the way he paid for her books.
examples.cn: 他的兄弟情谊表现在他为她付书钱的方式上。

examples.en: The fraternal twins were born twenty minutes apart.
examples.cn: 这对异卵双胞胎出生时间相差二十分钟。

examples.en: The union sent a fraternal greeting to the striking miners.
examples.cn: 工会向罢工的矿工送去了兄弟般的问候。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗特诺」——兄弟并肩一站，情同手足：兄弟的、兄弟般的

root: 拉丁语 frater（兄弟）→ fraternus（兄弟般的）→ 中世纪拉丁语 fraternalis → 英语 fraternal；同族词有 fraternity、fraternize、fraternization，并与本族语词 brother 同出印欧语重构形式 bhrater。

sensesIntro.en: Fraternal moves from a real brother, to brotherly kindness, to two-egg twins, to clubs, nations, religious houses, equal comrades and linked parties.
sensesIntro.cn: fraternal 从真正的兄弟，到兄弟般的善意，再到异卵双生、社团、国家、修士团体、平等的同伴与相连的政党。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two brothers of the same height standing side by side, shoulders touching.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个一样高的兄弟并肩而立，手臂搭在彼此肩上。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: the literal sense of belonging to a brother.
branches.cn: 家庭线：属于兄弟的字面义。

branches.en: THE FEELING: brotherly kindness offered to anyone, not only to kin.
branches.cn: 情感线：兄弟般的善意可以给任何人，不只给亲人。

branches.en: THE WOMB: two eggs make a brother pair before birth.
branches.cn: 母腹线：两个卵子在出生之前就凑成一对兄弟。

branches.en: THE HOUSE OF BROTHERS: clubs and religious communities both copy the family.
branches.cn: 兄弟之家线：社团与宗教团体都在模仿家庭。

branches.en: THE WIDER WORLD: nations, colleagues and parties borrow the same image.
branches.cn: 更广的世界线：国家、同事与政党借用同一个意象。

intro.en: Fraternal is a Latin brother word; English adds suffixes to build fraternity, fraternize and fraternization.
intro.cn: fraternal 是拉丁语中表示兄弟的词；英语加后缀构成 fraternity、fraternize 与 fraternization。

latinIntro.en: Latin frater and fraternus are recorded, and fraternalis belongs to medieval Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 frater 与 fraternus 均有记录，fraternalis 属于中世纪拉丁语。

items.example: The noun is the head of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整个词族的中心。

items.example: The adjective adds the quality of a brother.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词加上「兄弟」的性质。

items.example: The medieval form passes straight into English.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪的词形直接传入英语。
英语保留了拉丁语词形。

items.example: The suffix -ity turns the adjective into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 把形容词变成名词。
它构成 fraternity。

items.meaning: to act as brothers with others
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 构成这个动词。
它构成 fraternize。
后缀 -ation 指这一动作。
它构成 fraternization。

definition_zh: 亲善交往；与…打成一片；与敌方人员私下交往
definition_en: to spend time with other people in a friendly way, especially with those one is not supposed to mix with
core_image: 两群人放下架子，围在一张桌边称兄道弟
scene: 战地营区里，几名士兵趁夜色与对面阵地的人交换香烟。Some soldiers fraternized with the men across the line under cover of night.
sceneCN: 这里 fraternize 是「与敌方人员私下交往」（第 2 个义项：与不该交往的人亲近）；句意：一些士兵趁夜色与对面阵地的人私下往来。

pos.zh: 亲善交往；与…友好相处

derivatives.zh: 由 fraternize 加后缀 -ation 构成，指亲善交往，尤指与敌方人员的私下往来

senses.title: To mix socially as friends
senses.definition: to spend time with other people in a friendly, informal way
senses.definitionCN: 以友好、随意的方式与他人相处
senses.example: She fraternizes easily with her new colleagues.
senses.exampleCN: 她很容易和新同事打成一片。
senses.why: The Latin root frater means brother, so fraternize begins as the act of treating other people like brothers.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 frater 意为「兄弟」，所以 fraternize 本指把别人当兄弟一样对待。

senses.title: To associate with the enemy
senses.definition: to have friendly contact with members of an opposing or hostile group, especially against rules
senses.definitionCN: 与对立或敌对群体的成员友好接触，尤指违反规定时
senses.example: The officer was punished for fraternizing with the enemy.
senses.exampleCN: 那名军官因与敌方人员私下交往而受罚。
senses.why: Once the brotherly verb entered military speech, its warmth became suspicious when it was directed at the other side.
senses.whyCN: 当这个「兄弟般」的动词进入军事语境后，这份亲近一旦指向敌方，就变得可疑。

senses.title: To join a group as one of its members
senses.definition: to become accepted in a group by sharing its social life
senses.definitionCN: 通过参与群体的社交生活而被接纳
senses.example: New students were encouraged to fraternize with the older ones.
senses.exampleCN: 新生被鼓励与学长学姐打成一片。
senses.why: Sharing ordinary social life is the modern, neutral version of the old brotherly bond.
senses.whyCN: 共享日常社交生活，是古老「兄弟情谊」在现代的中性版本。

senses.title: To treat subordinates as equals
senses.titleCN: 与下属不分上下级地亲近
senses.definition: to be overly friendly with people of lower rank, so that authority becomes unclear
senses.definitionCN: 与级别较低者过于亲近，以致上下级界限模糊
senses.example: Senior officers were warned not to fraternize with the troops.
senses.exampleCN: 高级军官被警告不要与士兵不分上下地亲近。
senses.why: The brotherly image makes rank disappear, and that is exactly what disciplined institutions fear.
senses.whyCN: 「兄弟」的意象让等级消失，而这正是强调纪律的机构所担心的。

intro.en: Fraternize comes from Latin frater, brother, through fraternus and Medieval Latin fraternizare, then French fraterniser.
intro.cn: fraternize 源自拉丁语 frater（兄弟），经 fraternus 与中世纪拉丁语 fraternizare，再经法语 fraterniser 进入英语。

items.en: Frater means brother, the family word behind fraternal and fraternity.
items.cn: frater 意为「兄弟」，是 fraternal 与 fraternity 背后的家庭词。

items.en: Fraternus means brotherly or of a brother.
items.cn: fraternus 意为「兄弟的、兄弟般的」。

items.en: Fraternizare means to make or treat as a brother.
items.cn: fraternizare 意为「使成为兄弟、以兄弟相待」。

items.en: French fraterniser carries the verb into wider social use.
items.cn: 法语 fraterniser 把这个动词带入更广泛的社交用法。

items.en: English fraternize appears in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语 fraternize 于十七世纪出现。

items.en: Modern English adds the military and workplace senses of mixing with others.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了与敌方、与同僚交往的军事与职场义项。

note.en: Fraternize is the verb of brotherly mixing, close to its noun and adjective family and to ordinary words for social contact.
note.cn: fraternize 是表示「兄弟般交往」的动词，与它的名词、形容词同族词以及普通社交词相邻。

entries.definition: a brotherhood or a student society
entries.definitionCN: 兄弟情谊；大学联谊会

entries.definition: brotherly
entries.definitionCN: 兄弟的；兄弟般的

entries.definition: the act of mixing socially with others
entries.definitionCN: 亲善交往；与敌方人员的私下往来

entries.definition: to mix with other people at a social event
entries.definitionCN: 在社交场合与人交往

entries.definition: to spend time with someone as a companion
entries.definitionCN: 与…交往；结伴

entries.definition: to spend time with people that others disapprove of
entries.definitionCN: 与不受欢迎的人厮混（含贬义）

normalIntro.en: Fraternize is built on the Latin word for brother, so every sense is about treating other people as close companions.
normalIntro.cn: fraternize 建立在拉丁语「兄弟」一词上，因此每个义项都与把他人当作亲密同伴有关。

normal.en: Fraternize with someone means to treat them like a friend or brother.
normal.cn: fraternize with someone 就是把对方当作朋友或兄弟。

normal.en: Soldiers who fraternize with the enemy face punishment.
normal.cn: 与敌方人员私下交往的士兵会受罚。

normal.en: The noun fraternization often appears in military reports.
normal.cn: 名词 fraternization 常出现在军事报告里。

normal.en: New staff fraternize with colleagues at the coffee machine.
normal.cn: 新员工在咖啡机旁与同事打成一片。

normal.en: Compare socialize: fraternize stresses closeness, while socialize merely stresses contact.
normal.cn: 对比 socialize：fraternize 强调亲近，socialize 只强调接触。

abstract.en: Picture two men from opposite camps sharing a cigarette in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象敌对两边的人在黑暗中分一支烟。

abstract.en: Imagine a warm handshake across a front line that should not be crossed.
abstract.cn: 想象一只温暖的手越过本不该跨越的战线握过来。

abstract.en: Think of a newcomer being pulled into a circle of laughing coworkers.
abstract.cn: 想象一个新人被拉进一圈大笑的同事中。

examples.en: The soldiers were forbidden to fraternize with the local militia.
examples.cn: 士兵们被禁止与当地民兵私下交往。

examples.en: He fraternized with the villagers and soon learned their customs.
examples.cn: 他与村民打成一片，很快了解了他们的习俗。

examples.en: Fraternization between officers and enlisted men is against the rules.
examples.cn: 军官与士兵之间不分上下地亲近违反规定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗拉特奈兹」——谐音「兄弟一块儿闹」，联想与兄弟打成一片；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 frater（兄弟）→ fraternus（兄弟般的）→ 中世纪拉丁语 fraternizare（以兄弟相待）→ 法语 fraterniser → 英语 fraternize，核心义「把外人当兄弟」。

sensesIntro.en: Fraternize starts as friendly brotherly mixing, then splits into group acceptance, forbidden contact with the enemy, and over-familiarity with subordinates.
sensesIntro.cn: fraternize 从兄弟般的友好交往出发，随后分出融入群体、与敌方私通以及与管理对象过于亲近等义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two strangers treating each other like brothers.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个陌生人以兄弟相待。

branches.en: Friendly social mixing is the plain sense.
branches.cn: 友好的社交往来是最基本的义项。

branches.en: The same warmth turned toward an enemy becomes a charge.
branches.cn: 同样的亲近一旦朝向敌方，就成了一条罪状。

branches.en: Being accepted by a group is the neutral modern extension.
branches.cn: 被群体接纳是现代中性的延伸义。

branches.en: Too much brotherhood with subordinates erases rank.
branches.cn: 与下属过分称兄道弟会抹掉等级。

branches.en: Both senses describe people choosing to share ordinary social life.
branches.cn: 这两个义项都指人们主动共享日常社交生活。

intro.en: Fraternize is a Latin brother word: frater supplies the root, and the verb suffix -ize turns the noun idea into an action.
intro.cn: fraternize 是一个拉丁语「兄弟」词：frater 提供词根，动词后缀 -ize 把名词概念变成动作。

latinIntro.en: Latin frater means brother, and fraternus means brotherly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 frater 意为「兄弟」，fraternus 意为「兄弟般的」。

items.exampleCN: frater 是这个词族的根。
fraternus 提供形容词词干。

items.example: Medieval Latin fraternizare is the verb source.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪拉丁语 fraternizare 是动词来源。

items.example: French fraterniser passes the verb to English.
items.exampleCN: 法语 fraterniser 把该动词传给英语。
拉丁语 fraternitas 指这种情谊。

items.example: Fraternity comes through the same root.
items.exampleCN: fraternity 出自同一词根。
后缀 -ize 构成 fraternize。
fraternize 保留「兄弟般交往」的动作义。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的名词后缀
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 fraternization。

items.meaningCN: 亲善交往；与敌方私下往来
items.exampleCN: fraternization 指这一行为。
